title.zh: 卷二百七十三 列傳第三十二 李進卿 楊美 何繼筠 李漢超 郭進 牛思進 李謙溥 姚內斌 董遵誨 賀惟忠 馬仁瑀
title.en: Volume 273 Biographies 32: Li Jinqing, Yang Mei, He Jiyun, Li Hanchao, Guo Jin, Niu Sijin, Li Qianpu, Yao Neibin, Dong Zunhui, He Weizhong, Ma Renyu
title.raw: 卷二百七十三 列傳第三十二 李進卿 楊美 何繼筠 李漢超 郭進 牛思進 李謙溥 姚內斌 董遵誨 賀惟忠 馬仁瑀 Volume 273 Biographies 32: Li Jinqing, Yang Mei, He Jiyun, Li Hanchao, Guo Jin, Niu Sijin, Li Qianpu, Yao Neibin, Dong Zunhui, He Weizhong, Ma Renyu

sentences.zh: 李進卿

translations.literal: Li Jinqing
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinqing

sentences.zh: 李進卿，幷州晉陽人。

translations.literal: Li Jinqing was a man of Jinyang in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinqing was a native of Jinyang in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少以驍勇隸護聖軍。

translations.literal: In youth, because of his fierceness and bravery, he was enrolled in the Husheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he joined the Husheng Army for his martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，杜重威帥師敗安重榮於宗城，進卿力戰有功，擢為興順軍校。

translations.literal: In Tianfu of Later Jin, Du Chongwei commanded troops and defeated An Chongrong at Zongcheng; Jinqing fought vigorously with merit and was promoted to squad commander in the Xingshun Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Later Jin's Tianfu era, when Du Chongwei routed An Chongrong at Zongcheng, Jinqing distinguished himself in the fighting and was made a squad commander in the Xingshun Army.

sentences.zh: 周祖開國，命領所部兵戍靈壽，久之，遷龍捷指揮使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Zhou founded the state, he was ordered to lead his command and garrison Lingshou; after a long time, he was transferred to Dragon Swift command commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou's founding emperor took power, he was sent to garrison Lingshou at the head of his troops; years later he became commissioner of the Dragon Swift command.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，從世宗戰高平，改鐵騎指揮使，歷散員左射都校，改鐵騎及內殿直都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, he followed Emperor Shizong in the battle at Gaoping, was changed to Iron Cavalry command commissioner, served as left archery squad chief in the casual corps, and was changed to deputy chief of both Iron Cavalry and Inner Hall Straight.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiande era he fought with Emperor Shizong at Gaoping, then served as Iron Cavalry commander, left archery chief of the casual corps, and deputy chief of both the Iron Cavalry and the Inner Hall Straight.

sentences.zh: 宋初，領貴州刺史，三遷鐵騎左廂都指揮使，領乾州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he held the post of prefect of Gui prefecture, was thrice promoted to left wing Iron Cavalry command commissioner, and held the post of Qianzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Song he governed Gui prefecture, rose through three posts to command the left wing of the Iron Cavalry, and served as Qianzhou regimentation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，遷控鶴左廂都指揮使，改漢州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande, he was transferred to left wing Crane Control command commissioner and changed to Hanzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qiande era he took command of the left wing of the Crane Control corps and became Hanzhou regimentation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉虎捷左廂都指揮使，領澄州團練使。

translations.literal: In year two, he was transferred to left wing Tiger Swift command commissioner and held the post of Chengzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made commander of the left wing of the Tiger Swift corps and Chengzhou regimentation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬，伐蜀，以進卿為歸州路行營步軍都指揮使，拔巫山砦，下夔、萬二州。

translations.literal: That winter, in the campaign against Shu, Jinqing was made field army infantry command commissioner on the Guizhou route; he captured the Wushan stockade and took the two prefectures of Kuai and Wan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, during the Shu campaign, Jinqing commanded the infantry of the Guizhou route field army, seized the Wushan stockade, and captured Kuai and Wan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，錄功拜侍衛親軍步軍都虞候，領保順軍節度。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, his merit was recorded and he was appointed deputy chief of the palace guard infantry and given the Baoshun military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell, he was rewarded with the post of deputy chief of the palace guard infantry and the Baoshun military governorship.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，太祖親征河東，留進卿為在京都巡檢，潁州刺史常暉、淄州刺史韓光愿分為河南、北巡檢。

translations.literal: In year two of Kaibao, Emperor Taizu personally campaigned in Hedong and left Jinqing as capital patrol inspector; Chang Hui, prefect of Ying prefecture, and Han Guangyuan, prefect of Zi prefecture, were respectively made Henan and northern patrol inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao year two, when Emperor Taizu marched on Hedong in person, Jinqing was left as capital patrol inspector while Chang Hui of Ying prefecture and Han Guangyuan of Zi prefecture patrolled Henan and the north.

sentences.zh: 及還，改親軍馬軍都虞候。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, he was changed to deputy chief of the palace guard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's return he became deputy chief of the palace guard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷步軍都指揮使，領靜江軍節度，卒，年五十九，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In year six, he was transferred to infantry command commissioner, held the Jingjiang military governorship, died at age fifty-nine, and was posthumously given the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made infantry commander and Jingjiang military governor; he died at fifty-nine and was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子延渥、延信。

translations.literal: His sons were Yanwo and Yanxin.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Yanwo and Yanxin.

sentences.zh: 延信至內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Yanxin rose to the Inner Hall Honored Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxin rose to serve in the Inner Hall Honored Corps.

sentences.zh: 子 延渥

translations.literal: Son: Yanwo
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yanwo

sentences.zh: 延渥以蔭補供奉官，尋為閤門祗候，三遷至西京左藏庫使。

translations.literal: Yanwo entered service by hereditary privilege as a tribute officer, soon became a gate attendant, and was thrice promoted to manager of the Western Capital left treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwo entered office by privilege as a tribute officer, became a gate attendant, and after three promotions was manager of the Western Capital left treasury.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，歷知平戎、寧邊、順安軍、保州、威虜軍鈐轄，又知冀州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, he successively governed Pingrong, Ningbian, and Shun'an garrisons, Baozhou, and Weilu garrison as military controller, and also governed Ji prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianping era he served as military controller at Pingrong, Ningbian, Shun'an, Baozhou, and Weilu, and later governed Ji prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，徙瀛州。

translations.literal: In year six, he was transferred to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，契丹大舉擾邊，經胡盧河，踰關南，十月，抵城下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, the Khitan raided the frontier on a large scale, passed through the Hulu River, crossed south of the pass, and in the tenth month reached the foot of the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era the Khitan launched a major border raid, crossed the Hulu River and the pass to the south, and in the tenth month reached the city walls.

sentences.zh: 晝夜鼓噪，四面夾攻。

translations.literal: Day and night they beat drums and shouted, attacking from all four sides at once.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night they beat drums and shouted, pressing the attack from every side.

sentences.zh: 旬日，其勢益張，唯擊鼓伐木之聲相聞，驅奚人負板秉燭乘墉而上。

translations.literal: After ten days their force grew stronger; only the sounds of drum-beating and tree-felling could be heard, as they drove Xi tribesmen carrying boards and holding torches to climb the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days their assault intensified; drumbeats and the crash of felled timber filled the air as Xi tribesmen, boards on their backs and torches in hand, scaled the walls.

sentences.zh: 延渥率州兵強壯，又集巡檢史普所部乘城，發礧石巨木擊之，皆纍纍而墜，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Yanwo led the strong men of the prefectural army and also gathered the troops under patrol inspector Shi Pu to man the walls, hurling boulders and great logs at them; they fell in heaps, and casualties were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwo rallied the prefecture's strongest troops and Shi Pu's patrol force to the walls, raining boulders and timber on the attackers; enemy soldiers fell in heaps and casualties were heavy.

sentences.zh: 翌日，契丹主與其母親鼓眾急擊，發矢如雨。

translations.literal: The next day the Khitan ruler and his mother personally beat drums and urged the troops in a fierce assault; arrows flew like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Khitan ruler and his mother personally drummed the troops forward in a furious assault, and arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 延渥分兵拒守益堅，契丹遁去，死者三萬餘，傷者倍之，獲鎧甲、兵矢、竿牌數百萬，驛書以聞。

translations.literal: Yanwo divided his troops and defended with increasing firmness; the Khitan fled. The dead numbered more than thirty thousand, the wounded twice that number; armor, weapons, arrows, poles, and shields in the millions were captured, and a courier report was sent.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwo held the line with divided forces and growing resolve until the Khitan withdrew; more than thirty thousand were killed and twice as many wounded, and millions of pieces of armor, weapons, and equipment were taken. A courier report was dispatched.

sentences.zh: 賜延渥錦袍、金帶，將士緡錢，遷延渥本州團練使。

translations.literal: Yanwo was granted a brocade robe and gold belt, the officers and soldiers were given cash, and Yanwo was transferred to regimentation commissioner of his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwo received a brocade robe and gold belt, his troops were rewarded with cash, and he was promoted to regimentation commissioner of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以通判、太子中允陸元凱為國子博士，賜緋；

translations.literal: Assistant prefect and Palace Attendant Lu Yuankai was made Doctor of the National University and granted crimson robes;
translations.idiomatic: Assistant prefect Lu Yuankai, a Palace Attendant, was made Doctor of the National University and granted crimson robes;

sentences.zh: 推官李翔為太子中允；

translations.literal: judicial aide Li Xiang was made Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: judicial aide Li Xiang was made Palace Attendant;

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍蔡亨為右讚善大夫；

translations.literal: recording secretary Cai Heng was made Right Supporter of Goodness Grand Master;
translations.idiomatic: recording secretary Cai Heng was made Right Supporter of Goodness Grand Master;

sentences.zh: 侍禁、兵馬監押王誨，殿直、貝冀同巡檢史普為內殿崇班充職如故。

translations.literal: attendant guard and horse troop supervisor Wang Hui, and palace attendant and joint Beiji patrol inspector Shi Pu were made Inner Hall Honored Corps while retaining their posts.
translations.idiomatic: attendant guard and horse troop supervisor Wang Hui and joint Beiji patrol inspector Shi Pu were promoted to the Inner Hall Honored Corps while keeping their posts.

sentences.zh: 初，戍棚垂板護城才數寸許，契丹射之，矢集其上凡二百餘。

translations.literal: At first the garrison shed had hanging boards protecting the wall only a few inches thick; the Khitan shot at them, and more than two hundred arrows lodged in them.
translations.idiomatic: At first the garrison's hanging wall-shields were only a few inches thick; the Khitan riddled them with more than two hundred arrows.

sentences.zh: 及請葺城，詔取板視之，真宗頗稱其勞。

translations.literal: When repairs to the city were requested, an edict ordered the boards brought for inspection, and Emperor Zhenzong greatly praised their labors.
translations.idiomatic: When the city repairs were proposed, the emperor ordered the arrow-studded boards brought for inspection, and Emperor Zhenzong praised their efforts.

sentences.zh: 又聞城守之際，陸元凱流矢中面，史普勇敢不避敵，復遷元凱屯田員外郎、普尚食副使。

translations.literal: It was also learned that during the defense Lu Yuankai was struck in the face by a stray arrow and Shi Pu fought bravely without shunning the enemy; Yuankai was again promoted to outer office director of garrison fields and Pu to deputy commissioner of the imperial kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Lu Yuankai had been struck in the face by a stray arrow during the siege while Shi Pu fought fearlessly, the court promoted Yuankai to outer office director of garrison fields and Pu to deputy commissioner of the imperial kitchen.

sentences.zh: 普尋卒，又錄其子昭度為右侍禁，昭儉為奉職。

translations.literal: Pu soon died, and his sons Zhaodu and Zhaojian were recorded for office as right attendant guard and service officer respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu soon died, and his sons Zhaodu and Zhaojian were granted posts as right attendant guard and service officer.

sentences.zh: 二年，延渥徙知邢州，歷天雄軍、貝州副都部署，知冀、貝、博三州。

translations.literal: In year two, Yanwo was transferred to govern Xingzhou, served as deputy commander of Tianxiong Army and Beizhou, and governed the three prefectures of Ji, Bei, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Yanwo was made prefect of Xingzhou, served as deputy commander at Tianxiong and Beizhou, and governed Ji, Bei, and Bo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符八年入朝，以疾，連賜告，換右領軍衛大將軍，領演州團練使。

translations.literal: In year eight of Dazhong Xiangfu he came to court; because of illness he was repeatedly granted leave, was changed to great general of the Right Leading Army Guard, and held the post of Yanzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu year eight he came to court; illness brought repeated leave, and he was reassigned as great general of the Right Leading Army Guard and Yanzhou regimentation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，從其請，以左武衛大將軍致仕。

translations.literal: The next year, acceding to his request, he retired as great general of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, at his request, he retired with the rank of great general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Tianxi era.

sentences.zh: 子宗禹，為內殿崇班。

translations.literal: His son Zongyu served in the Inner Hall Honored Corps.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongyu served in the Inner Hall Honored Corps.

sentences.zh: 楊美，幷州文水人。

translations.literal: Yang Mei was a man of Wenshui in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Mei was a native of Wenshui in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 本名光美，避太宗舊名改焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Guangmei; it was changed to avoid the former name of Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Guangmei, he changed his name to avoid the taboo on Emperor Taizong's former name.

sentences.zh: 美狀貌雄偉，武力絕人，以豪俠自任。

translations.literal: Mei had a grand and imposing appearance, martial strength beyond others, and took upon himself the role of a bold knight-errant.
translations.idiomatic: Mei was imposing in stature, unmatched in strength, and styled himself a bold man of honor.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，周祖征三叛，美杖策詣軍門求見，周祖召與語，壯之，留帳下。

translations.literal: In Qianyou of Later Han, when Emperor Gaozu of Zhou campaigned against the Three Rebellions, Mei came staff in hand to the army gate seeking an audience; the emperor summoned him to speak, admired him, and kept him in his retinue.
translations.idiomatic: During Later Han's Qianyou era, when Zhou's founding emperor marched against the Three Rebellions, Mei came staff in hand to the camp gate and asked to see him; impressed, the emperor kept him in his retinue.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，累遷禁軍大校，從世宗征淮南，以功擢鐵騎都指揮使，領白州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun, he was repeatedly promoted in the palace guard to senior commander; he followed Emperor Shizong in the Huainan campaign and, for merit, was promoted to Iron Cavalry command commissioner and given the post of prefect of Bai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun era he rose through the palace guard ranks, fought with Emperor Shizong in Huainan, and for his service was made Iron Cavalry commander and prefect of Bai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖與美有舊，即位，以為內殿直都知。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu and Mei had an old acquaintance; upon his accession he appointed Mei director of Inner Hall Straight.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu and Mei were old acquaintances; when Taizu took the throne he made Mei director of the Inner Hall Straight.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，升青州北海縣為軍，以美為軍使。

translations.literal: In year three of Jianlong, Beihai county in Qing prefecture was elevated to a garrison, and Mei was made garrison commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong year three, Beihai county in Qing prefecture was raised to a garrison, and Mei was made its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 為政尚簡易，民皆德之。

translations.literal: In governing he favored simplicity and ease, and the people all regarded him with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was plain and easy, and the people held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，召還，北海民數百詣闕乞留，詔諭之不去，笞為首者始罷。

translations.literal: In year two of Qiande he was recalled; several hundred people of Beihai went to the palace gate begging that he be kept; an edict reasoned with them but they would not leave, and only when the ringleaders were flogged did they desist.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande year two he was recalled, but hundreds of Beihai residents petitioned at court to keep him; even after an imperial edict they refused to leave, and only flogging the ringleaders ended the protest.

sentences.zh: 遷馬步軍都頭。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief of horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief of the horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 會討蜀，以美為歸州路戰棹左右廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Shu was being attacked, Mei was made left and right wing battle-oar command commissioner on the Guizhou route.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shu campaign he was made commander of both wings of the battle fleet on the Guizhou route.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，遷內外馬步軍副都軍頭，領恩州團練使。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was transferred to deputy chief of inner and outer horse and foot armies and given the post of Enzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he became deputy chief of the inner and outer horse and foot armies and Enzhou regimentation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，改領端州防禦使。

translations.literal: In year two of Kaibao, he was changed to defense commissioner of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao year two he became defense commissioner of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，加都軍頭，領宣州觀察使。

translations.literal: In year six, he was given the additional post of army chief and held the post of observation commissioner of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made army chief and observation commissioner of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄授虎捷左右廂都指揮使，領河西軍節度。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed left and right wing Tiger Swift command commissioner and given the Hexi military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of both wings of the Tiger Swift corps and given the Hexi military governorship.

sentences.zh: 會遣党進、潘美征太原，命美為行營馬軍都虞候。

translations.literal: When Dang Jin and Pan Mei were sent to campaign against Taiyuan, Mei was ordered to be field army cavalry deputy chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Dang Jin and Pan Mei were sent against Taiyuan, Mei was made deputy chief of the field army cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年冬，出為保靜軍節度。

translations.literal: In the winter of year two of Taiping Xingguo, he went out as Baojing military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Taiping Xingguo year two he was posted as Baojing military governor.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，以疾求解官歸京師，尋醫藥，詔遣內侍與道士馬志視之。

translations.literal: In the summer of year three, because of illness he requested to resign and return to the capital to seek medicine; an edict sent an inner attendant and the Daoist Ma Zhi to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year, ill, he asked to resign and return to the capital for treatment; the emperor sent an inner attendant and the Daoist Ma Zhi to care for him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年四十八，贈侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he died at age forty-eight and was posthumously given the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at forty-eight and was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 命中使護葬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered an inner attendant to oversee the burial.
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant was ordered to oversee his burial.

sentences.zh: 美為人任氣好施，凡得予賜及奉祿，盡賙給親戚故舊。

translations.literal: Mei as a man was proud-spirited and generous; whatever he received in grants and salary he entirely distributed to relatives and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Mei was proud and generous by nature; he gave away every grant and every paycheck to kin and old friends.

sentences.zh: 死之日，家無餘財，人多歎息之。

translations.literal: On the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth, and many people sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his household had nothing left, and many mourned the fact.

sentences.zh: 何繼筠

translations.literal: He Jiyun
translations.idiomatic: He Jiyun

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，升棣州為團練，以繼筠充使。

translations.literal: In year two of Jianlong, Di prefecture was elevated to regimentation status, and Jiyun was made commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong year two, Di prefecture was raised to regimentation status and Jiyun was made its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，命為關南兵馬都監。

translations.literal: In year three, he was ordered to be frontier south horse and foot army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made supervisor of the Guannan horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，加本州防禦使。

translations.literal: In year four of Qiande, he was given the additional post of defense commissioner of his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande year four he was also made defense commissioner of his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開寶元年秋，命昭義節度李繼勳等征太原，以繼筠為先鋒部署。

translations.literal: In the autumn of year one of Kaibao, Li Jixun of Zhaoyi military governorship and others were ordered to campaign against Taiyuan, and Jiyun was made vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Kaibao year one, when Li Jixun of Zhaoyi and others were sent against Taiyuan, Jiyun was made vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 至渦河，與幷人遇，擊走之，奪汾河橋，敗其眾於城下，獲馬五百匹，擒其將張環、石贇以獻。

translations.literal: Reaching the Wo River, he encountered the men of Bing and drove them off, seized the Fen River bridge, defeated their forces below the city, captured five hundred horses, and took their generals Zhang Huan and Shi Yun captive to present.
translations.idiomatic: At the Wo River he met the Jin forces, drove them off, seized the Fen River bridge, and routed them below the city; he captured five hundred horses and took the generals Zhang Huan and Shi Yun.

sentences.zh: 二年春，太祖親征晉陽，契丹來援。

translations.literal: In the spring of year two, Emperor Taizu personally campaigned against Jinyang, and the Khitan came to aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year Emperor Taizu marched on Jinyang in person, and the Khitan came to its aid.

sentences.zh: 繼筠時屯兵陽曲縣，驛召至行在所，授以方略，命將精騎數千赴石嶺關拒契丹，謂之曰：「翌日亭午，俟卿來奏捷也。

translations.literal: Jiyun was then encamped at Yangqu county; he was summoned by courier to the imperial camp, given a strategy, and ordered to lead several thousand picked cavalry to Shiling Pass to block the Khitan. The emperor said to him: "Tomorrow at noon I await your report of victory."
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun was then encamped at Yangqu county; summoned by courier to the imperial camp, he was given his orders and told to lead several thousand elite cavalry to Shiling Pass to block the Khitan. The emperor said, "Tomorrow at noon I expect your victory report."

sentences.zh: 」至期，帝御北臺以俟。

translations.literal: When the time came, the emperor mounted the northern platform to wait.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed hour the emperor took his place on the northern platform to wait.

sentences.zh: 見一騎自北來，亟遣逆問之，乃繼筠子承睿來獻捷。

translations.literal: Seeing a single rider coming from the north, he quickly sent someone to meet and inquire; it was Jiyun's son Chengrui coming to present the victory report.
translations.idiomatic: When a lone rider appeared from the north, he sent someone to meet him at once; it was Jiyun's son Chengrui bearing news of victory.

sentences.zh: 生擒刺史二人，獲生口百餘，斬首千餘級，馬七百餘匹，器甲甚眾。

translations.literal: Two prefects were taken alive, more than a hundred captives were seized, more than a thousand heads were cut off, more than seven hundred horses were taken, and weapons and armor were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Two prefects were taken alive, more than a hundred captives seized, over a thousand heads counted, more than seven hundred horses captured, and a great quantity of arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 初，幷人恃契丹為聲援，及捷奏，太祖命以所獲首級、鎧甲示城下，幷人喪氣。

translations.literal: At first the men of Bing relied on the Khitan as vocal support; when the victory report arrived, Emperor Taizu ordered the captured heads and armor displayed below the city, and the men of Bing lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin defenders had counted on Khitan support; when the victory report came, Emperor Taizu had the captured heads and armor displayed before the walls, and their morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 繼筠以功拜建武軍節度、判棣州。

translations.literal: For his merit Jiyun was appointed Jianwu military governor and given concurrent authority over Di prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this victory Jiyun was made Jianwu military governor with concurrent authority over Di prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，來朝，詔賜鞍馬、戎杖，令戍邊。

translations.literal: In year three he came to court; an edict granted him saddle horse and military staff and ordered him to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he came to court, received saddle horse and military staff, and was ordered back to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，來朝，疽發背。

translations.literal: In the autumn of year four he came to court, and a carbuncle broke out on his back.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year he came to court, and a carbuncle erupted on his back.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸其第，錫齎甚厚。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage visited his residence, and gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited his home and bestowed lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: Before long he died at age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 帝親臨之，為之流涕，從容謂侍臣曰：「繼筠捍邊有功，朕不早授方鎮者，慮其數奇耳。

translations.literal: The emperor personally attended him, wept for him, and calmly said to the attending ministers: "Jiyun had merit in defending the frontier; the reason I did not early grant him a regional command was that I feared his fate would be unlucky."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attended him in person, wept, and told his ministers, "Jiyun served the frontier with distinction; I delayed giving him a regional command because I feared his luck would run out."

sentences.zh: 今才領節制，果至淪沒，良可惜也。

translations.literal: Now he had just received military authority and indeed came to ruin — truly a pity.
translations.idiomatic: He had only just taken command, and now he is gone — a great loss."

sentences.zh: 」贈侍中，賻絹五百匹，中使護喪，令以生平所佩劍及介胄同葬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Palace Attendant, five hundred bolts of burial silk, an inner attendant to oversee the funeral, and ordered to be buried with the sword and armor he had worn in life.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, given five hundred bolts of burial silk, and an inner attendant was sent to oversee the funeral; he was buried with the sword and armor he had worn in life.

sentences.zh: 繼筠深沉有智略，前後備邊二十年，與士卒同甘苦，得其死力。

translations.literal: Jiyun was deep and reserved with wisdom and strategy; for twenty years before and after he guarded the frontier, sharing hardship and comfort with the soldiers and winning their utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun was shrewd and deliberate; for twenty years on the frontier he shared hardship with his men and won their utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 善揣邊情，邊人畏伏，多畫像祠之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at gauging frontier conditions; frontier people feared and submitted to him, and many painted his portrait to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: He read the border situation well; frontier peoples feared and respected him, and many painted his portrait for worship.

sentences.zh: 子承矩。

translations.literal: His son was Chengju.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chengju.

sentences.zh: 子 承矩

translations.literal: Son: Chengju
translations.idiomatic: Son: Chengju

sentences.zh: 米信知滄州，以其不習吏事，命承矩知節度副使，實專郡治。

translations.literal: Mi Xin governed Cangzhou; because he was unskilled in administrative affairs, Chengju was ordered to serve as deputy military governor, in fact holding sole charge of prefectural governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi Xin governed Cangzhou but lacked skill in civil administration, Chengju was made deputy military governor and in practice ran the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時契丹撓邊，承矩上疏曰：「臣幼侍先臣關南征行，熟知北邊道路、川源之勢。

translations.literal: At the time the Khitan harassed the frontier; Chengju submitted a memorial saying: "In youth I attended my late father on Guannan campaigns and am thoroughly familiar with northern frontier roads and the lay of rivers and terrain."
translations.idiomatic: As the Khitan harassed the frontier, Chengju submitted a memorial: "In youth I followed my late father on Guannan campaigns and know the northern roads and terrain well."

sentences.zh: 若於順安砦西開易河蒲口，導水東注於海，東西三百餘里，南北五七十里，資其陂澤，築堤貯水為屯田，可以遏敵騎之奔軼。

translations.literal: If at the west of Shun'an stockade the Yi River mouth at Pukou were opened, water guided east to pour into the sea, spanning more than three hundred li east to west and fifty to seventy li north to south, using its marshes and lakes, building dikes to store water for garrison fields — this could check the enemy cavalry's swift raids.
translations.idiomatic: If we opened the Yi River at Pukou west of Shun'an stockade and channeled its waters east to the sea across three hundred li east-west and fifty to seventy li north-south, we could use the marshes to build dikes, store water, and create garrison fields that would block enemy cavalry raids.

sentences.zh: 俟期歲間，關南諸泊悉壅闐，即播為稻田。

translations.literal: Wait a full year, and all the lakes of Guannan would be filled to the brim, then sown as rice fields.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year the Guannan lakes would fill, and we could sow them as rice fields.

sentences.zh: 其緣邊州軍臨塘水者，止留城守軍士，不煩發兵廣戍。

translations.literal: For frontier prefectures and garrisons bordering the ponded waters, only garrison soldiers need be kept; there would be no need to dispatch troops for broad garrisoning.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrisons along the impounded waters would need only city garrisons, without wide deployments of troops.

sentences.zh: 收地利以實邊，設險固以防塞，春夏課農，秋冬習武，休息民力，以助國經。

translations.literal: Gather the land's profit to strengthen the frontier, set up defenses to guard the passes, assign farming in spring and summer and drill in arms in autumn and winter, rest the people's strength, and thereby aid the state's economy.
translations.idiomatic: We would harvest the land's bounty to strengthen the frontier, build defenses to guard the passes, farm in spring and summer and drill in autumn and winter, spare the people's strength, and bolster the state's resources.

sentences.zh: 如此數年，將見彼弱我強，彼勞我逸，此禦邊之要策也。

translations.literal: Thus for several years, one would see them weak and us strong, them weary and us at ease — this is the essential strategy for defending the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In a few years the enemy would grow weak while we grew strong, weary while we rested — the essential strategy for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 其順安軍以西，抵西山百里許，無水田處，亦望選兵戍之，簡其精銳，去其冗繆。

translations.literal: From Shun'an garrison westward, reaching the western mountains for about a hundred li where there is no paddy land, it is also hoped that picked troops be garrisoned there, selecting the elite and removing the redundant.
translations.idiomatic: West of Shun'an garrison, for a hundred li to the western mountains where there is no paddy, I also ask that picked troops be posted — elite forces only, with the redundant removed.

sentences.zh: 夫兵不患寡，患驕慢而不精；

translations.literal: As for troops, one does not worry about their being few, but about their being arrogant and undisciplined rather than elite;
translations.idiomatic: Armies need not fear being few, but being arrogant and undisciplined;

sentences.zh: 將不患怯，患偏見而無謀。

translations.literal: as for generals, one does not worry about their being timid, but about their being narrow-minded and without strategy.
translations.idiomatic: generals need not fear timidity, but narrow-mindedness and lack of strategy.

sentences.zh: 若兵精將賢，則四境可以高枕而無憂。

translations.literal: If troops are elite and generals worthy, then the four borders can rest on high pillows without worry.
translations.idiomatic: With elite troops and worthy generals, the realm could rest secure on every border.

sentences.zh: 」太宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong praised the plan and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 屬霖雨為災，典者多議其非便。

translations.literal: Continuous rain brought disaster, and those in charge mostly debated that it was not expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains brought disaster, and many officials argued the plan was impractical.

sentences.zh: 承矩引援漢、魏至唐屯田故事，以折眾論，務在必行。

translations.literal: Chengju cited precedents of garrison fields from Han, Wei, and through Tang to refute the various opinions, insisting that it must be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Chengju cited garrison-field precedents from Han through Tang to counter the objections and pressed for the plan to go forward.

sentences.zh: 乃以承矩為制置河北緣邊屯田使，俾董其役。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengju was made frontier garrison-field commissioner for the Hebei border and charged with overseeing the work.
translations.idiomatic: Chengju was then appointed frontier garrison-field commissioner for the Hebei border and put in charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 事具《食貨志》。

translations.literal: The matter is fully recorded in the "Treatise on Food and Commodities."
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the "Treatise on Food and Commodities."

sentences.zh: 由是自順安以東瀕海，廣袤數百里，悉為稻田，而有莞蒲蜃蛤之饒，民賴其利。

translations.literal: From this, from Shun'an eastward along the coast, for several hundred li in breadth and length, all became rice fields, and there was abundance of rushes, reeds, clams, and oysters; the people relied on its profit.
translations.idiomatic: From Shun'an east to the coast, hundreds of li became rice fields rich in rushes, reeds, clams, and oysters, and the people prospered.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，擢為西上閤門使、知滄州，逾年，徙雄州。

translations.literal: In year four of Chunhua, he was promoted to western upper gate envoy and given charge of Cangzhou; after a year he was transferred to Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua year four he became western upper gate envoy and prefect of Cangzhou; a year later he was transferred to Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 御書印紙錄其功最，仍賜以弓劍。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote on sealed paper recording his foremost merit and also granted him bow and sword.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote his outstanding service on sealed paper and granted him bow and sword.

sentences.zh: 承矩推誠御眾，同其甘苦。

translations.literal: Chengju treated the masses with sincerity and shared their hardship and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Chengju led his men with sincerity and shared their hardships.

sentences.zh: 邊民有告機事者，屏左右與之款接，無所猜忌，故契丹動息皆能前知。

translations.literal: When frontier people reported intelligence, he dismissed attendants and received them warmly without suspicion; thus he could know Khitan movements in advance.
translations.idiomatic: When border residents brought intelligence, he dismissed his attendants and received them openly; thus he learned Khitan movements before they happened.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，契丹精騎數千夜襲城下，伐鼓縱火，以逼樓堞。

translations.literal: In year one of Zhidao, several thousand Khitan elite cavalry raided the city at night, beating drums and setting fires to press against the towers and battlements.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao year one, several thousand Khitan elite cavalry raided the city at night, beating drums and setting fires to press the walls.

sentences.zh: 承矩整兵出拒，遲明，列陣酣戰久之，斬馘甚眾，擒其酋所謂鐵林相公者，契丹遁去。

translations.literal: Chengju marshaled troops and went out to resist; at dawn he formed ranks and fought fiercely for a long time, beheading very many, captured their chieftain called the Iron Forest Duke, and the Khitan fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chengju marched out to meet them; at dawn his lines fought fiercely for hours, killing many and capturing their chieftain, the so-called Iron Forest Duke, and the Khitan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是年春，府州嘗敗契丹眾，承矩條殺獲以諭州民，或揭於市，契丹愧忿，故有是役。

translations.literal: That spring, Fuzhou had once defeated Khitan forces; Chengju listed the kills and captures to inform the prefectural people, and some were posted in the market; the Khitan were shamed and enraged, hence this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Fuzhou had defeated Khitan forces; Chengju posted the tally of kills and captures for the people, some in the market square, shaming the Khitan and provoking this raid.

sentences.zh: 太宗意其輕率致寇，復命與滄州安守忠兩換其任。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong thought he had been rash and brought on the raid, and again ordered him to exchange posts with An Shouzhong of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong blamed his rashness for provoking the raid and ordered him to swap posts with An Shouzhong of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏廷式使河北，得雄州功狀，抗表上言。

translations.literal: Wei Tingshi was envoy to Hebei, obtained the Xiongzhou merit report, and submitted a forthright memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tingshi, on mission to Hebei, obtained the Xiongzhou merit report and submitted a forthright memorial.

sentences.zh: 又遣內侍劉核實，及麾下士有功者千餘人，皆進擢齎賜。

translations.literal: An inner attendant Liu was also sent to verify the facts, and more than a thousand soldiers under his command who had merit were all promoted and given gifts.
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant named Liu was sent to verify the facts, and more than a thousand of Chengju's men who had served with merit were promoted and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，復遣知雄州，賜承矩詔曰：「朕嗣守鴻業，惟懷永圖，思與華夷共臻富壽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, he again sent him to govern Xiongzhou and granted Chengju an edict saying: "I inherit and guard the great enterprise, ever cherishing long-range plans, thinking to bring Chinese and barbarians together to reach wealth and longevity."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, he sent Chengju back to Xiongzhou with an edict: "I inherit the great enterprise and seek lasting peace, hoping that Chinese and barbarians alike may prosper."

sentences.zh: 而契丹自太祖在位之日，先帝繼統之初，和好往來，禮幣不絕。

translations.literal: Yet from the days when Emperor Taizu was on the throne and at the beginning when the former emperor succeeded, friendly relations and exchanges of gifts and tribute had not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Taizu's reign through my predecessor's accession, friendly exchanges and gifts had never ceased with the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 其後克復汾、晉，疆臣貪地，為國生事，信好不通。

translations.literal: Afterward the recovery of Fen and Jin, frontier ministers greedy for land, created trouble for the state, and trust and friendship were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Fen and Jin were recovered, greedy frontier officials stirred trouble for the state and good relations broke down.

sentences.zh: 今者聖考上仙，禮當訃告。

translations.literal: Now the sacred predecessor has ascended to immortality, and by ritual death should be announced.
translations.idiomatic: Now that my sacred predecessor has passed, propriety requires that his death be announced.

sentences.zh: 汝任居邊要，洞曉詩書，凡有事機，必能詳究，輕重之際，務在得中。

translations.literal: You hold a post at a critical frontier, thoroughly understand the classics, and for any situation can surely investigate in detail; in matters of weight and lightness, strive to hit the mean.
translations.idiomatic: You hold a critical frontier post and know the classics well; weigh every situation carefully and strike the right balance.

sentences.zh: 」承矩貽書契丹，諭以懷來之旨，然未得其要。

translations.literal: Chengju sent a letter to the Khitan, explaining the intent of winning them over, but did not get the essential point across.
translations.idiomatic: Chengju wrote to the Khitan explaining the court's conciliatory intent, but failed to win them over.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，契丹南侵，屢遣內侍以密詔問禦遏之計，密封以獻。

translations.literal: In year two of Xianping, the Khitan invaded south; inner attendants were repeatedly sent with secret edicts asking plans for blocking them, and sealed reports were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping year two, as the Khitan invaded south, inner attendants repeatedly brought secret edicts asking for blocking plans, and Chengju submitted sealed reports.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔聽邊民越拒馬河塞北市馬。

translations.literal: An edict once permitted frontier people to cross the Horse-Rejection River north of the barrier to buy horses in the market.
translations.idiomatic: An edict once allowed frontier residents to cross the Horse-Rejection River north of the barrier to buy horses.

sentences.zh: 承矩上言曰：「緣邊戰棹司自淘河至泥姑海口，屈曲九百餘里，此天險也。

translations.literal: Chengju submitted a memorial saying: "The frontier battle-oar office from the Tao River to the Nigu estuary, winding for more than nine hundred li — this is heaven's barrier."
translations.idiomatic: Chengju submitted a memorial: "The frontier battle fleet patrols from the Tao River to the Nigu estuary, winding more than nine hundred li — a natural barrier."

sentences.zh: 太宗置砦二十六，鋪百二十五，廷臣十一人，戍卒三千餘，部舟百艘，往來巡警，以屏奸詐，則緩急之備，大為要害。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong established twenty-six stockades, one hundred twenty-five posts, eleven court officials, more than three thousand garrison soldiers, and a fleet of one hundred boats patrolling back and forth to screen against treachery — thus preparations for emergency were a great strategic key.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong established twenty-six stockades, 125 posts, eleven court officials, more than three thousand garrison troops, and a fleet of one hundred boats to patrol against treachery — a vital emergency defense.

sentences.zh: 今聽公私貿市，則人馬交度，深非便宜，且砦、鋪皆為虛設矣。

translations.literal: Now if public and private trade is permitted, then men and horses would cross back and forth — deeply inexpedient, and the stockades and posts would all become empty establishments.
translations.idiomatic: Allowing public and private trade would let men and horses cross freely — highly inexpedient — and render the stockades and posts meaningless.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，即停前詔，屢被手劄褒飭。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the previous edict was immediately halted, and he was repeatedly praised in personal notes.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was accepted, the previous edict was revoked, and he received repeated praise in personal notes from the emperor.

sentences.zh: 三年，召還，拜引進使。

translations.literal: In year three, he was recalled and appointed introduction commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled and made introduction commissioner.

sentences.zh: 州民百餘詣闕貢馬，乞借留承矩，詔書嘉獎，復遣之。

translations.literal: More than a hundred prefectural people went to the palace gate presenting horses, begging to retain Chengju on loan; an edict praised them and sent him back again.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred residents petitioned at court with horses, asking to keep Chengju; an edict praised them and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 承矩上言曰：

translations.literal: Chengju submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chengju submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「契丹輕而不整，貪而無親，勝不相讓，敗不相救。

translations.literal: "The Khitan are light and undisciplined, greedy and without loyalty; in victory they do not yield to one another, in defeat they do not rescue one another."
translations.idiomatic: "The Khitan are undisciplined and greedy, with no loyalty among themselves; in victory they yield to no one, in defeat they rescue no one."

sentences.zh: 以馳騁為容儀，以弋獵為耕釣。

translations.literal: They take galloping as proper deportment and hunting as farming and fishing.
translations.idiomatic: They treat galloping as decorum and hunting as farming and fishing.

sentences.zh: 櫛風沐雨，不以為勞；

translations.literal: Combing the wind and bathing in rain, they do not consider it labor;
translations.idiomatic: Wind and rain do not weary them;

sentences.zh: 露宿草行，不以為苦。

translations.literal: sleeping in the dew and traveling through grass, they do not consider it hardship.
translations.idiomatic: sleeping in the open and traveling through grass do not trouble them.

sentences.zh: 復恃騎戰之利，故頻年犯塞。

translations.literal: Again relying on the advantage of cavalry warfare, they therefore year after year violate the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on cavalry, they raid the frontier year after year.

sentences.zh: 臣聞兵有三陣：日月風雲，天陣也；

translations.literal: I have heard that armies have three arrays: sun, moon, wind, and clouds are the heaven array;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that armies have three arrays: sun, moon, wind, and clouds form the heaven array;

sentences.zh: 山陵水泉，地陣也；

translations.literal: mountains, hills, water, and springs are the earth array;
translations.idiomatic: mountains, hills, water, and springs form the earth array;

sentences.zh: 兵車士卒，人陣也。

translations.literal: chariots, troops, and soldiers are the human array.
translations.idiomatic: chariots, troops, and soldiers form the human array.

sentences.zh: 今用地陣而設險，以水泉而作固，建設陂塘，綿亙滄海，縱有敵騎，安能折衝？

translations.literal: Now using the earth array to set up defenses, using water and springs to make fortifications, building ponds and dikes stretching across the blue sea — even if there were enemy cavalry, how could they clash and charge?
translations.idiomatic: If we use terrain for defense, water for fortification, and build ponds and dikes stretching to the sea, what enemy cavalry could break through?

sentences.zh: 昨者契丹犯邊，高陽一路，東負海，西抵順安，士庶安居，即屯田之利也。

translations.literal: When the Khitan recently violated the frontier, the Gaoyang route, east backed by the sea and west reaching Shun'an — officials and commoners dwelt in peace; this is the profit of garrison fields.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan recently raided, the Gaoyang route from the sea to Shun'an remained secure — the benefit of garrison fields.

sentences.zh: 今順安西至西山，地雖數軍，路才百里，縱有丘陵岡阜，亦多川瀆泉源，因而廣之，制為塘埭，自可息邊患矣。

translations.literal: Now from Shun'an west to the western mountains, though the land spans several garrisons, the route is only a hundred li; even if there are hills and mounds, there are also many streams and springs — expanding them accordingly and making ponds and dikes could naturally end frontier troubles.
translations.idiomatic: From Shun'an west to the mountains, though several garrisons span the route, the distance is only a hundred li; with its hills and many streams, expanding ponds and dikes there could end frontier troubles.

sentences.zh: 今緣邊守將多非其才，不悅詩書，不習禮樂，不可守疆界。

translations.literal: Now many frontier garrison generals are not suited to their posts; they do not delight in the classics, do not practice ritual and music — they cannot guard the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Too many frontier commanders lack the talent for their posts; ignorant of the classics and untrained in ritual, they cannot hold the borders.

sentences.zh: 制御無方，動誤國家，雖提貔虎之師，莫遏犬羊之眾。

translations.literal: Without method in control, they constantly err against the state; though leading tiger-and-leopard armies, they cannot check the multitude of dogs and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Without proper command they harm the state; even with elite armies they cannot stop the barbarian hordes.

sentences.zh: 臣按兵法，凡用兵之道，校之以計而索其情，謂將孰有能，天地孰得，法令孰行，兵眾孰強，士卒孰練，賞罰孰明，此料敵制勝之道也。

translations.literal: I examine military law: in all ways of using troops, compare by calculation and seek the circumstances — which general has ability, which side gains heaven and earth, which laws are enforced, which forces are strong, which soldiers are trained, which rewards and punishments are clear — this is the way to assess the enemy and achieve victory.
translations.idiomatic: Military doctrine teaches us to compare and assess: which general is capable, which side holds the advantage, which laws are enforced, which army is strong, which soldiers are trained, which rewards and punishments are clear — this is how to defeat the enemy.

sentences.zh: 知此而用戰者必勝，否則必敗。

translations.literal: Those who know this and go to war will surely win; otherwise they will surely lose.
translations.idiomatic: Those who know this will win; those who do not will lose.

sentences.zh: 夫惟無慮而易敵者必擒於人也。

translations.literal: Only those without forethought who treat the enemy lightly will surely be captured by others.
translations.idiomatic: Only the thoughtless who underestimate the enemy will be captured.

sentences.zh: 伏望慎擇疆吏，出牧邊民，厚之以奉祿，使悅其心，借之以威權，使嚴其令。

translations.literal: I humbly hope that frontier officials be carefully chosen to go out and shepherd border people, enriched with salary to please their hearts, lent authority to enforce their orders strictly.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that frontier officials be carefully chosen, paid well to win their loyalty, and granted authority to enforce strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 然後深溝高壘，秣馬厲兵，為戰守之備。

translations.literal: Then dig deep moats and raise high ramparts, feed horses and sharpen weapons, and make preparations for fighting and defending.
translations.idiomatic: Then dig deep moats, raise high walls, feed the horses, sharpen weapons, and prepare for both attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 修仁立德，布政行惠，廣安輯之道。

translations.literal: Cultivate benevolence and establish virtue, spread governance and practice kindness, and broaden the way of peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivate benevolence, govern with kindness, and broaden the path to peace.

sentences.zh: 訓士卒，辟田疇，勸農耕，畜芻粟，以備凶年。

translations.literal: Train soldiers, open fields, encourage farming, store fodder and grain to prepare for bad years.
translations.idiomatic: Train the troops, open fields, encourage farming, and store grain and fodder against famine.

sentences.zh: 完長戟，修勁弩，謹烽燧，繕保戍，以防外患。

translations.literal: Complete long halberds, repair strong crossbows, attend carefully to beacon fires, repair garrison defenses to guard against external trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Maintain halberds, repair crossbows, tend the beacon fires, and repair garrison defenses against external threats.

sentences.zh: 來則禦之，去則備之，如此則邊城按堵矣。

translations.literal: When they come, resist them; when they leave, prepare against them — thus frontier cities will be settled and secure.
translations.idiomatic: Resist them when they come, prepare when they leave — and the frontier will be secure.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞古之明王，安集吏民，順俗而教，簡募良材，以備不虞。

translations.literal: I further hear that ancient enlightened kings settled officials and people, taught according to custom, and selectively recruited fine talent to prepare against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient enlightened kings settled their people, taught according to custom, and selectively recruited talent against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 齊桓、晉文皆募兵以服鄰敵，故強國之君，必料其民有膽勇者聚為一卒，樂進戰效力以顯忠勇者聚為一卒，能逾高赴遠、輕足善鬥者聚為一卒，此三者兵之練銳，內出可以決圍，外入可以屠城。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin both recruited troops to subdue neighboring enemies; thus rulers of strong states must assess their people — those with courage and bravery gathered into one corps, those who delight in advancing to fight and show loyalty gathered into one corps, those who can cross heights and go far, light of foot and skilled in combat gathered into one corps — these three are the army's trained elite; going out within they can break sieges, going in without they can storm cities.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin recruited troops to subdue neighbors; strong states gather the courageous, the eager fighters, and the swift and skilled into three elite corps that can break sieges from within and storm cities from without.

sentences.zh: 況小大異形，強弱異勢，險易異備。

translations.literal: Moreover, small and large differ in form, strong and weak differ in circumstance, difficult and easy differ in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Small and large states differ in form, strong and weak in circumstance, difficult and easy terrain in preparation.

sentences.zh: 卑身以事強，小國之形也。

translations.literal: Humbling oneself to serve the strong is the form of a small state.
translations.idiomatic: Humbling oneself before the strong is the way of a small state.

sentences.zh: 以蠻夷伐蠻夷，中國之形也。

translations.literal: Using barbarians to attack barbarians is the form of the Central State.
translations.idiomatic: Using barbarians to fight barbarians is the way of the Central State.

sentences.zh: 故陳湯統西域而郅支滅，常惠用烏孫而邊部寧。

translations.literal: Thus Chen Tang commanded the Western Regions and Zhizhi was destroyed; Chang Hui used the Wusun and the frontier regions were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tang commanded the Western Regions and destroyed Zhizhi; Chang Hui used the Wusun and pacified the frontier.

sentences.zh: 且聚膽勇、樂戰、輕足之徒，古稱良策，請試行之。

translations.literal: Moreover, gathering the bold, battle-eager, and light-footed — anciently called a fine strategy — I ask that it be tried.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering the bold, battle-eager, and swift — an ancient strategy — I ask that it be tried.

sentences.zh: 且邊鄙之人，多負壯勇，識外邦之情偽，知山川之形勝。

translations.literal: Moreover, frontier people mostly possess bold courage, know the truth and falsehood of foreign states, and know the strategic terrain of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier people are mostly brave, know foreign lands well, and understand the strategic terrain.

sentences.zh: 望於邊郡置營召募，不須品度人才，止求少壯有武藝者萬人。

translations.literal: I hope that camps be established in frontier prefectures for recruitment, without needing to grade talent, only seeking ten thousand young and strong with martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that recruitment camps be set on the frontier, seeking ten thousand young, strong men with martial skill, without grading talent.

sentences.zh: 俟契丹有警，令智勇將統而用之，必顯成功，乃中國之長算也。

translations.literal: When the Khitan give alarm, order wise and brave generals to command and use them — success will surely be shown; this is the Central State's long-range plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan threaten, wise and brave generals should command them — success is assured; this is the Central State's long-term strategy.

sentences.zh: 又如榷場之設，蓋先朝從權立制，以惠契丹，縱其渝信犯盟，亦不之廢，似全大體。

translations.literal: Again, as for establishing frontier markets — the former court established the system expediently to benefit the Khitan; even if they violated trust and broke the covenant, it was not abolished, seemingly preserving the larger propriety.
translations.idiomatic: As for frontier markets, the former court established them expediently to benefit the Khitan; even when they broke faith, the markets were not abolished, preserving the larger propriety.

sentences.zh: 今緣邊榷場，因其犯塞，尋即停罷。

translations.literal: Now frontier markets, because of their border violations, are immediately halted.
translations.idiomatic: Now frontier markets are shut down as soon as the Khitan raid the border.

sentences.zh: 去歲以臣上言，於雄州置場賣茶，雖貲貨並行，而邊氓未有所濟。

translations.literal: Last year, based on my memorial, a market was set at Xiongzhou to sell tea; though goods and commodities went together, frontier commoners received no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, on my recommendation, a tea market was opened at Xiongzhou; though trade flowed, frontier commoners gained little.

sentences.zh: 乞延訪大臣，議其可否，或文武中有抗執獨議，是必別有良謀。

translations.literal: I beg that great ministers be consulted to debate its feasibility; if among civil and military officials there are those who hold firm independent views, they surely have other fine plans.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that great ministers debate the plan; if any civil or military official holds a firm independent view, he may have a better strategy.

sentences.zh: 請委之邊任，使施方略，責以成功。

translations.literal: Please entrust them with frontier duties, let them apply strategy, and hold them accountable for success.
translations.idiomatic: Entrust them with frontier duties, let them apply their strategies, and hold them accountable for results.

sentences.zh: 苟空陳浮議，上惑聖聰，秖如靈州，足為證驗，況茲契丹又非夏州之比也。」

translations.literal: If empty floating opinions are offered, confusing the sacred hearing — Lingzhou alone suffices as proof; moreover, this Khitan is not comparable to Xiazhou."
translations.idiomatic: Empty talk that confuses the throne has been disproved at Lingzhou alone; moreover, the Khitan are not like the Xiazhou Tanguts."

sentences.zh: 四年十月，建議選銳兵於乾寧軍，挽刀魚船自界河直趣平州境，以牽西面之勢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of year four, he proposed selecting elite troops at Qianning garrison, using knife-oar fish boats from the border river straight toward Pingzhou territory to draw off western forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year he proposed selecting elite troops at Qianning garrison to send knife-oar boats from the border river toward Pingzhou and draw off western Khitan forces.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔兼領制置屯田使。

translations.literal: In year five, an edict ordered him to concurrently hold the post of garrison-field commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was ordered to concurrently serve as garrison-field commissioner.

sentences.zh: 始建榷場，或者謂承矩意在繼好，然契丹無厭，未足誠信，徒使公行窺伺。

translations.literal: When the frontier market was first established, some said Chengju's intent was to continue good relations, but the Khitan were insatiable, not worthy of trust, and it only allowed open spying.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier market opened, some said Chengju sought continued good relations, but the insatiable Khitan could not be trusted and used it for open espionage.

sentences.zh: 會契丹有殺斥候卒者，復罷之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan killed scout soldiers, it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan killed scout soldiers, the market was closed again.

sentences.zh: 時契丹數窺邊城，大浚渠，頗撓其役。

translations.literal: At the time the Khitan repeatedly spied on frontier cities; they greatly dredged canals and considerably disrupted the work.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan repeatedly spied on frontier cities and dredged canals, considerably disrupting the project.

sentences.zh: 詔承矩握兵深入其境，以分其勢。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chengju to grasp troops and penetrate deep into their territory to divide their force.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Chengju to lead troops deep into Khitan territory to divide their forces.

sentences.zh: 承矩以無騎兵，第遣數千卒出混泥城，襲之而還。

translations.literal: Chengju, having no cavalry, merely sent several thousand soldiers out from Hunni city, raided, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking cavalry, Chengju sent several thousand soldiers from Hunni city on a raid and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，入朝，進領英州團練使。

translations.literal: In year one of Jingde, he came to court and was advanced to hold the post of Yingzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde year one he came to court and was promoted to Yingzhou regimentation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 真宗謂宰相曰：「承矩讀書好名，以才能自許，宜擇善地處之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said to the chief ministers: "Chengju reads books and loves reputation, considers himself talented — a good post should be chosen for him."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong told his chief ministers, "Chengju is learned and ambitious; find a good post for him."

sentences.zh: 」冬，出知澶州。

translations.literal: That winter, he went out to govern Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was posted as prefect of Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 承矩自守邊以來，嘗欲朝廷懷柔遠人，為息兵之計。

translations.literal: Since guarding the frontier, Chengju had wished the court would treat distant peoples with kindness and make plans to cease warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the frontier, Chengju had urged the court to treat distant peoples with kindness and seek peace.

sentences.zh: 及是，車駕按巡本部，卒與契丹和，益加歎賞。

translations.literal: At this time the imperial carriage inspected his jurisdiction, and peace with the Khitan was finally achieved; praise was increased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor inspected his jurisdiction and peace with the Khitan was achieved, Chengju received still greater praise.

sentences.zh: 韓杞之至也，命郊勞之。

translations.literal: When Han Qi arrived, he was ordered to be welcomed at the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi arrived, Chengju was ordered to welcome him at the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 明年春，復知雄州。

translations.literal: The next spring, he again governed Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he returned as prefect of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，契丹始遣使奉幣。

translations.literal: That year, the Khitan for the first time sent envoys presenting tribute gifts.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Khitan sent envoys with tribute gifts for the first time.

sentences.zh: 承矩以朝廷待邊人之禮悠久可行者，悉疏以聞。

translations.literal: Chengju memorialized all the court's long-standing feasible protocols for treating frontier peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Chengju memorialized all long-standing court protocols for treating frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 手詔嘉納，仍聽事有未盡者便宜裁處。

translations.literal: A personal edict praised and accepted it, and still permitted him to decide expediently on matters not yet fully settled.
translations.idiomatic: A personal edict praised the report and authorized him to decide expediently on unfinished matters.

sentences.zh: 三年，真拜雄州團練使。

translations.literal: In year three, he was truly appointed Xiongzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was formally appointed Xiongzhou regimentation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時邊兵稍息，農政未修。

translations.literal: At the time frontier warfare had slightly subsided, but agricultural administration was not yet restored.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier warfare had subsided, but agriculture had not yet recovered.

sentences.zh: 又置緣邊安撫使，命承矩為之，且詔邊民誘其復業。

translations.literal: A frontier pacification commissioner was also established, Chengju was ordered to hold the post, and an edict also urged frontier people to return to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: A frontier pacification commissioner was established with Chengju in the post, and an edict urged border residents to return to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 承矩曰：「契丹聞之，必謂誘其部屬也。

translations.literal: Chengju said: "If the Khitan hear of this, they will surely think we are enticing their subjects."
translations.idiomatic: Chengju said, "The Khitan will think we are enticing their subjects."

sentences.zh: 」乃易詔文為水旱流民之意。

translations.literal: Thereupon he changed the edict text to refer to flood, drought, and displaced people.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the edict to refer to flood, drought, and displaced people instead.

sentences.zh: 王欽若時知樞密，援漢蟲達、周仲居改詔，請罪承矩。

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo was then director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; citing Han Chongsui and Zhou Zhongju altering edicts, he requested punishment for Chengju.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo, then director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, citing precedents of Han Chongsui and Zhou Zhongju altering edicts, asked that Chengju be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「承矩任邊有功，當優假之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Chengju has merit on the frontier; he should be treated with leniency."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Chengju has served the frontier with merit; he should be treated leniently."

sentences.zh: 」第詔自今朝旨未便者，奏稟進止。

translations.literal: An edict merely ordered that from today, where imperial intent was not convenient, he should memorialize for approval before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: An edict merely required that henceforth he memorialize for approval before acting on matters not clearly authorized.

sentences.zh: 承矩頗有識鑒，典長沙日，李沆、王旦為佐，承矩厚待之，以為有公輔器。

translations.literal: Chengju had considerable discernment; when governing Changsha, Li Hang and Wang Dan were his assistants — Chengju treated them generously, thinking they had the capacity for chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Chengju was discerning; when governing Changsha he treated assistants Li Hang and Wang Dan generously, recognizing their capacity for high office.

sentences.zh: 善推步，自知冥數，乃以老疾求僻郡。

translations.literal: Skilled in astronomical calculation, knowing his fate, he then because of age and illness requested a remote prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in astronomy and aware of his fate, he requested a remote prefecture because of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 詔自擇其代，承矩以李允則為請。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to choose his own replacement; Chengju requested Li Yunze.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to choose his own successor, Chengju recommended Li Yunze.

sentences.zh: 乃授承矩齊州團練使，遣之任，至郡裁七日，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengju was appointed Qizhou regimentation commissioner, sent to his post; reaching the prefecture, only seven days passed before he died at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Chengju was appointed Qizhou regimentation commissioner; he reached his post and died seven days later at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 特贈相州觀察使，賻錢五十萬，絹五百匹，中使護葬。

translations.literal: He was specially posthumously given the title of Xiangzhou observation commissioner, five hundred thousand in burial money, five hundred bolts of silk, and an inner attendant to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Xiangzhou observation commissioner, given five hundred thousand in burial funds and five hundred bolts of silk, and an inner attendant oversaw the funeral.

sentences.zh: 以其子龜齡為侍禁；

translations.literal: His son Guiling was made attendant guard;
translations.idiomatic: His son Guiling was made attendant guard;

sentences.zh: 昌齡、九齡為殿直；

translations.literal: Changling and Jiuling were made palace attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Changling and Jiuling were made palace attendants;

sentences.zh: 遐齡為齋郎。

translations.literal: Xialing was made fast-officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xialing was made a fast-officer.

sentences.zh: 緣邊洎涿、易州民，聞承矩卒，皆相率詣雄州發哀飯僧。

translations.literal: Frontier people as far as Zhuo and Yi prefectures, hearing of Chengju's death, all in groups went to Xiongzhou to mourn and feed monks.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier residents as far as Zhuo and Yi prefectures, hearing of Chengju's death, gathered at Xiongzhou to mourn and feed monks.

sentences.zh: 昌齡娶齊王女太和縣主，至內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Changling married the Princess of Taihe county, daughter of the Prince of Qi, and rose to the Inner Hall Honored Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Changling married the Princess of Taihe, daughter of the Prince of Qi, and rose to the Inner Hall Honored Corps.

sentences.zh: 昌齡子象中，為閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Changling's son Xiangzhong served as a gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Changling's son Xiangzhong served as a gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 李漢超

translations.literal: Li Hanchao
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanchao

sentences.zh: 李漢超，雲州雲中人。

translations.literal: Li Hanchao was a man of Yunzhong in Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanchao was a native of Yunzhong in Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 始事鄴帥范延光，不為所知。

translations.literal: He first served Fan Yanguang, military governor of Ye, but was not recognized by him.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Fan Yanguang, military governor of Ye, but won no recognition.

sentences.zh: 又事鄆帥高行周，亦不見親信。

translations.literal: He then served Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Yan, but was also not treated with intimacy and trust.
translations.idiomatic: He then served Gao Xingzhou of Yan, but was likewise given no trust.

sentences.zh: 會周世宗鎮澶淵，漢超遂委質焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong of Zhou was stationed at Chanyuan, Hanchao then pledged his allegiance to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong of Zhou was posted at Chanyuan, Hanchao pledged himself to his service.

sentences.zh: 即位，補殿前指揮使，三遷殿前都虞候。

translations.literal: Upon his accession, Hanchao was appointed palace front command commissioner and was thrice promoted to palace front deputy chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne, Hanchao became palace front commander and rose through three posts to palace front deputy chief.

sentences.zh: 宋初，改散指揮都指揮使，領綿州刺史，累遷控鶴左廂都校，領恩州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was changed to casual corps command commissioner, held the post of prefect of Mian prefecture, was repeatedly promoted to left wing Crane Control squad chief, and held the post of Enzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Song he became casual corps commander and prefect of Mian, then rose to left wing chief of the Crane Control corps and Enzhou regimentation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從平李重進，尋遷齊州防禦使兼關南兵馬都監。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Li Chongjin, and soon was transferred to defense commissioner of Qizhou with concurrent duty as Guannan horse and foot army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Li Chongjin and was soon made defense commissioner of Qizhou and Guannan horse and foot supervisor.

sentences.zh: 漢超在關南，人有訟漢超強取其女為妾及貸而不償者，太祖召而問之曰：「汝女可適何人？

translations.literal: While Hanchao was at Guannan, someone sued him for forcibly taking his daughter as a concubine and for borrowing without repaying; Emperor Taizu summoned and questioned him, saying: "To whom could your daughter be married?"
translations.idiomatic: At Guannan, a man sued Hanchao for forcibly taking his daughter as a concubine and for an unpaid loan; Emperor Taizu summoned him and asked, "To whom could your daughter have been married?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「農家也。

translations.literal: He replied: "To a farming family."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "To a farming family."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「漢超未至關南，契丹如何？

translations.literal: He again asked: "Before Hanchao came to Guannan, how were the Khitan?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu asked again, "Before Hanchao came to Guannan, how were the Khitan?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「歲苦侵暴。

translations.literal: He said: "Year after year we suffered raids and violence."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Year after year we suffered raids and violence."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「今復爾耶？

translations.literal: He said: "Is it so again now?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu asked, "Is it so again now?"

translations.literal: He said: "No."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "No."

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「漢超，朕之貴臣也，為其妾不猶愈於農婦乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu said: "Hanchao is my honored minister — becoming his concubine is not still better than being a farmer's wife?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu said, "Hanchao is my honored minister — is being his concubine not better than being a farmer's wife?"

sentences.zh: 使漢超不守關南，尚能保汝家之所有乎？

translations.literal: If Hanchao did not guard Guannan, could you still protect what your household possessed?
translations.idiomatic: If Hanchao did not guard Guannan, could you still keep what your household owns?

sentences.zh: 」責而遣之。

translations.literal: He rebuked him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu rebuked him and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 密使諭漢超曰：「亟還其女並所貸，朕姑貰汝，勿復為也。

translations.literal: A secret envoy instructed Hanchao: "Quickly return his daughter and what was borrowed; I forgive you for now — do not do it again."
translations.idiomatic: A secret envoy told Hanchao, "Return his daughter and the loan at once; I forgive you this time — do not do it again."

sentences.zh: 不足於用，何不以告朕耶？

translations.literal: If you lack for use, why not tell me?
translations.idiomatic: If you are short of funds, why not tell me?"

sentences.zh: 」漢超感泣，誓以死報。

translations.literal: Hanchao wept with emotion and vowed to repay with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchao wept and vowed to repay the emperor with his life.

sentences.zh: 在郡十七年，政平訟理，吏民愛之，詣闕求立碑頌德。

translations.literal: In the prefecture for seventeen years, government was settled and lawsuits were resolved; officials and people loved him and went to court requesting a stele to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: For seventeen years in office his governance was fair and lawsuits were just; officials and people loved him and petitioned at court for a stele praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔率更令徐鉉撰文賜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu ordered Director of the Directorate of Astronomy Xu Xuan to compose the text and grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu ordered Xu Xuan, director of the Directorate of Astronomy, to compose the inscription.

sentences.zh: 霸州監軍馬仁瑀嘗兄事漢超，多自肆，擅發麾下卒入遼境，剽奪人口、羊馬，由是二將交惡。

translations.literal: Ma Renyu, army supervisor of Bazhou, had once treated Hanchao as an elder brother but was much self-indulgent, arbitrarily sending troops under his command into Liao territory to plunder people, sheep, and horses; thus the two generals became mutually hostile.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Renyu, army supervisor of Bazhou, had once treated Hanchao as an elder brother but acted with great license, sending troops into Liao territory to plunder people and livestock; the two generals became bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 太祖慮其生變，遣中使賜漢超、仁瑀金帛，令和解之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu feared trouble would arise and sent an inner attendant to grant Hanchao and Renyu gold and silk, ordering them to reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing trouble, Emperor Taizu sent an inner attendant with gold and silk and ordered Hanchao and Renyu to reconcile.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，遷應州觀察使、判齊州，仍為關南巡檢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he was transferred to observation commissioner of Yingzhou with concurrent authority over Qizhou, and still served as Guannan patrol inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he became observation commissioner of Yingzhou with authority over Qizhou and remained Guannan patrol inspector.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，卒於屯所。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of year two, he died at his garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year he died at his garrison post.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚悼惜，贈太尉、忠武軍節度，中使護葬。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong deeply mourned and regretted it, posthumously granting him Grand Marshal and the Zhongwu military governorship; an inner attendant oversaw the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong deeply mourned him, posthumously honoring him as Grand Marshal and Zhongwu military governor; an inner attendant oversaw the burial.

sentences.zh: 漢超善撫士卒，與之同甘苦，死之日，軍中皆流涕。

translations.literal: Hanchao was skilled at comforting soldiers and shared hardship and comfort with them; on the day of his death the entire army wept.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchao treated his soldiers well and shared their hardships; on the day he died the whole army wept.

sentences.zh: 子守恩。

translations.literal: His son was Shou'en.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shou'en.

sentences.zh: 子 守恩

translations.literal: Son: Shou'en
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shou'en

sentences.zh: 守恩，少驍果善戰，有父風。

translations.literal: Shou'en, in youth fierce and resolute and skilled in battle, had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Shou'en was fierce and skilled in battle from youth and had his father's fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 初補齊州牙職。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed to a Qizhou guard staff post.
translations.idiomatic: He first served on the guard staff at Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，太祖親征太原，漢超為北面行營都監，守恩從父軍中。

translations.literal: In year two of Kaibao, Emperor Taizu personally campaigned against Taiyuan; Hanchao was northern field army supervisor, and Shou'en followed his father in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao year two, when Emperor Taizu marched on Taiyuan, Hanchao was northern field army supervisor and Shou'en served in his father's command.

sentences.zh: 會契丹遣兵援河東，至定州西嘉山，將入土門，守恩領牙兵數千騎戰敗之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan sent troops to aid Hedong, reaching Jia Mountain west of Dingzhou and about to enter Tumen Pass, Shou'en led several thousand guard cavalry and defeated them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan troops came to aid Hedong and reached Jia Mountain west of Dingzhou, about to enter Tumen Pass, Shou'en led several thousand guard cavalry and routed them.

sentences.zh: 斬首三千級，獲戰馬、器甲甚眾，擒首領二十七人。

translations.literal: Three thousand heads were cut off, very many war horses and armor were captured, and twenty-seven chieftains were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand heads were counted, many horses and suits of armor were captured, and twenty-seven chieftains were taken.

sentences.zh: 隨漢超見於行在，賜戎服金帶、器幣、緡錢，太祖謂左右曰：「此稚子能若是，他日將帥才也。

translations.literal: Following Hanchao he was received at the imperial camp and granted military dress, gold belt, weapons, gifts, and cash; Emperor Taizu said to those beside him: "This young lad can do such things — someday he will be general material."
translations.idiomatic: He was presented at the imperial camp with military dress, a gold belt, weapons, gifts, and cash; Emperor Taizu told his attendants, "This young man can do such things — someday he will be a general."

sentences.zh: 」漢超卒，擢為驍猛軍校，累官至隴州刺史、知靈州。

translations.literal: When Hanchao died, he was promoted to squad chief in the Fierce Army and rose through posts to prefect of Long prefecture and governor of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanchao died he was promoted to squad chief in the Fierce Army and rose to prefect of Long prefecture and governor of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 與轉運使陳緯部芻糧過瀚海，為賊所邀，守恩及子廣文助教象之、隴州衙內指揮使望之、弟寄班守忠皆沒。

translations.literal: With transport commissioner Chen Wei he escorted fodder and grain across the Hanhai; they were intercepted by bandits, and Shou'en, his son Xiangzhi the assistant tutor in the Broad Learning Academy, Longzhou inner command commissioner Wangzhi, and his younger brother the guest officer Shouzhong all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting fodder and grain across the Hanhai with transport commissioner Chen Wei, he was ambushed by bandits; Shou'en, his son Xiangzhi, Longzhou inner commander Wangzhi, and his younger brother Shouzhong all perished.

sentences.zh: 真宗聞之震悼，特賜守恩洪州觀察使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong, hearing of it, was shocked and grieved and specially granted Shou'en the post of Hongzhou observation commissioner.
