translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong was shocked and grieved and posthumously granted Shou'en the title of Hongzhou observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 次子祐之、順之、用之、潤之、慶之、成之、藏之。

translations.literal: Second sons: Youzhi, Shunzhi, Yongzhi, Runzhi, Qingzhi, Chengzhi, and Cangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Other sons included Youzhi, Shunzhi, Yongzhi, Runzhi, Qingzhi, Chengzhi, and Cangzhi.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，移淄州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou, he was transferred to Zi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhou's Guangshun era he was transferred to Zi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年，吏民詣觀察使舉留。

translations.literal: In year two, officials and people went to the observation commissioner to recommend retaining him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year officials and residents petitioned the observation commissioner to keep him in office.

sentences.zh: 是秋，遷登州刺史。

translations.literal: That autumn, he was transferred to prefect of Deng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was made prefect of Deng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會群盜攻劫居民，進率鎮兵平之，部內清肅，民吏千餘人詣闕請立《屏盜碑》，許之。

translations.literal: When bandits attacked and plundered residents, Jin led garrison troops to pacify them; within his jurisdiction all was cleared and settled, and more than a thousand people, officials and commoners, went to court requesting the erection of a "Bandit-Suppression Stele" — permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits raided the populace, Jin led garrison troops to suppress them and restore order; more than a thousand officials and residents petitioned at court for a "Bandit-Suppression Stele," and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，移衛州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, he was transferred to Wei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiande era he was transferred to Wei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 衛、趙、邢、洺間多亡命者，以汲郡依山帶河，易為出沒，伺間椎剽，吏捕之輒遁去，故累歲不能絕其黨類。

translations.literal: Between Wei, Zhao, Xing, and Ming prefectures there were many fugitives; because Ji commandery lay against mountains and along rivers, it was easy for them to appear and vanish, waiting for opportunities to rob and plunder; when officials captured them they always escaped, so for years their bands could not be eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives were numerous between Wei, Zhao, Xing, and Ming prefectures; Ji commandery's mountains and rivers made raids easy and captures futile, and for years their bands could not be eliminated.

sentences.zh: 進備知其情狀，因設計發擿之，數月間剪滅無餘，郡民又請立碑記其事。

translations.literal: Jin fully knew their circumstances and therefore devised a plan to expose and arrest them; within several months they were cut down with none remaining, and the prefectural people again requested a stele to record the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing their ways, Jin devised a plan to expose and arrest them; within months they were wiped out, and the people again requested a commemorative stele.

sentences.zh: 改洺州團練使，有善政，郡民復詣闕請立碑頌德，詔左拾遺鄭起撰文賜之。

translations.literal: He was changed to Mingzhou regimentation commissioner; his governance was good, and the prefectural people again went to court requesting a stele to praise his virtue; an edict ordered Left Reminder Zheng Qi to compose the text and grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Made Mingzhou regimentation commissioner, he governed well; the people again petitioned for a stele praising his virtue, and Left Reminder Zheng Qi was ordered to compose the inscription.

sentences.zh: 進嘗於城四面植柳，壕中種荷芰蒲薍，後益繁茂。

translations.literal: Jin once planted willows on all four sides of the city and sowed lotus, water chestnut, bulrush, and cattail in the moat; afterward they grew ever more lush.
translations.idiomatic: Jin once planted willows around the city walls and lotus, water chestnuts, bulrushes, and cattails in the moat; they later grew ever more lush.

sentences.zh: 郡民見之有垂涕者，曰：「此郭公所種也。」

translations.literal: When prefectural people saw them some wept, saying: "These were planted by Lord Guo."
translations.idiomatic: Some residents wept when they saw them and said, "These were planted by Lord Guo."

sentences.zh: 建隆初，太祖親征澤、潞，遷本州防禦使，充西山巡檢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong, when Emperor Taizu personally campaigned in Ze and Lu, he was transferred to defense commissioner of his prefecture and appointed western mountain patrol inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianlong, when Emperor Taizu campaigned in Ze and Lu, Jin became defense commissioner of his prefecture and western mountain patrol inspector.

sentences.zh: 嘗與曹彬、王全斌入太原境，獲數千人。

translations.literal: He once entered Taiyuan territory with Cao Bin and Wang Quanbin and captured several thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: He once entered Taiyuan territory with Cao Bin and Wang Quanbin and captured several thousand people.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，太祖親征河東，以進為行營前軍馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In year two of Kaibao, when Emperor Taizu personally campaigned in Hedong, Jin was made field army vanguard cavalry command commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao year two, when Emperor Taizu marched on Hedong, Jin was made vanguard cavalry commander of the field army.

sentences.zh: 九年，命將征河東，以進為河東道、忻、代等州行營馬步軍都監，招徠山後諸州民三萬七千餘口。

translations.literal: In year nine, when generals were ordered to campaign in Hedong, Jin was made Hedong route and Xin, Dai, and other prefectures field army horse and foot army supervisor, and recruited more than thirty-seven thousand people from the various prefectures behind the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, during the Hedong campaign, Jin was made field army supervisor for the Hedong route and Xin and Dai prefectures and recruited more than thirty-seven thousand people from the mountain prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，領雲州觀察使、判邢州，仍兼西山巡檢，賜京城道德坊第一區。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he held the post of Yunzhou observation commissioner with concurrent authority over Xingzhou, still also serving as western mountain patrol inspector, and was granted the first residence in Daode Lane in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he became Yunzhou observation commissioner with authority over Xingzhou, remained western mountain patrol inspector, and received the first residence on Daode Lane in the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年，車駕將征太原，先命進分兵控石嶺關，為都部署，以防北邊。

translations.literal: In year four, when the imperial carriage was about to campaign against Taiyuan, Jin was first ordered to divide troops and hold Shiling Pass as overall commander to guard against the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, as the emperor prepared to march on Taiyuan, Jin was ordered to hold Shiling Pass as overall commander against the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 契丹果犯關，進大破之，又攻破西龍門砦，俘馘來獻，自是幷人喪氣。

translations.literal: The Khitan indeed violated the pass; Jin greatly defeated them, also captured the western Longmen stockade, and presented captives and severed heads; from this the men of Bing lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan did attack the pass; Jin routed them, captured the western Longmen stockade, and presented captives and heads; the Jin defenders' morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 時田欽祚護石嶺軍，恣為奸利諸不法事，進雖力不能禁，亦屢形於言。

translations.literal: At the time Tian Qinhuo guarded the Shiling army and wantonly committed all manner of illegal profiteering; though Jin lacked the power to forbid it, he repeatedly expressed it in words.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Qinhuo, guarding the Shiling garrison, committed all manner of illegal profiteering; Jin could not stop him but spoke out repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 進武人，性剛烈，戰功高，欽祚以他事侵之，心不能甘，自經死，年五十八，欽祚以暴卒聞。

translations.literal: Jin was a military man, fierce by nature, with high battle merit; Qinhuo harassed him on other matters; his heart could not accept it, and he hanged himself at age fifty-eight; Qinhuo reported it as sudden death.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was a fierce warrior with high battle merit; when Qinhuo harassed him on other matters he could not bear it and hanged himself at fifty-eight; Qinhuo reported it as sudden death.

sentences.zh: 太宗悼惜久之，贈安國軍節度，中使護葬。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong mourned and regretted it for a long time, posthumously granting the Anguo military governorship; an inner attendant oversaw the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong mourned him for a long time, posthumously granting the Anguo military governorship; an inner attendant oversaw the burial.

sentences.zh: 後頗聞其事。

translations.literal: Later the matter was somewhat heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Later the truth came to light.

sentences.zh: 因罷欽祚內職，出為房州團練使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qinhuo's inner court post was removed and he was sent out as Fangzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhuo was removed from his inner court post and sent out as Fangzhou regimentation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 進有材幹，輕財好施，然性喜殺，士卒小違令，必寘於死，居家御婢僕亦然。

translations.literal: Jin had talent and ability, was light with wealth and generous in giving, yet by nature loved killing; if soldiers slightly violated orders he invariably put them to death, and at home in managing maids and servants it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was capable and generous, but by nature he was quick to kill; the slightest breach of orders by soldiers or servants meant death.

sentences.zh: 進在西山，太祖遣戍卒，必諭之曰：「汝輩謹奉法。

translations.literal: When Jin was in the western mountains, whenever Emperor Taizu sent garrison soldiers he always instructed them: "You must carefully obey the law."
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was in the western mountains, Emperor Taizu always warned newly posted garrison soldiers, "Obey the law carefully.

sentences.zh: 我猶貸汝，郭進殺汝矣。

translations.literal: I may still spare you, but Guo Jin will kill you."
translations.idiomatic: I may spare you, but Guo Jin will kill you."

sentences.zh: 」其御下嚴毅若此。

translations.literal: Thus stern and resolute was his command of subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the stern discipline with which he ruled his men.

sentences.zh: 然能以權道任人，嘗有軍校自西山詣闕誣進者，太祖詰知其情狀，謂左右曰：「彼有過畏罰，故誣進求免爾。

translations.literal: Yet he could employ men by expedient means; once a military officer from the western mountains came to court to falsely accuse Jin; Emperor Taizu questioned and learned the circumstances and said to those beside him: "He had an offense and feared punishment, so he falsely accused Jin seeking exemption."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could use men shrewdly; once an officer from the western mountains came to court to falsely accuse Jin; Emperor Taizu learned the truth and told his attendants, "He had committed an offense and feared punishment, so he falsely accused Jin to escape it."

sentences.zh: 」遣使送與進，令殺之。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy to deliver him to Jin and ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent him back to Jin and ordered Jin to kill him.

sentences.zh: 會幷人入寇，進謂誣者曰：「汝敢論我，信有膽氣。

translations.literal: When the men of Bing invaded, Jin said to the accuser: "You dared to speak against me — truly you have bold spirit."
translations.idiomatic: When Jin forces invaded, Jin told the accuser, "You dared to speak against me — you have real nerve.

sentences.zh: 今捨汝罪，能掩殺幷寇，即薦汝於朝；

translations.literal: Now I pardon your offense; if you can ambush and kill Jin bandits, I will recommend you to the court;"
translations.idiomatic: I pardon you now; if you can ambush and kill the Jin raiders, I will recommend you to the court;

sentences.zh: 如敗，可自投河東。

translations.literal: if you fail, you may go surrender yourself in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: if you fail, surrender yourself to Hedong."

sentences.zh: 」其人踴躍聽命，果致克捷。

translations.literal: That man eagerly accepted the order and indeed achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: The man eagerly accepted and indeed won the victory.

sentences.zh: 進即以聞，乞遷其職，太祖從之。

translations.literal: Jin immediately reported it and requested his promotion; Emperor Taizu acceded.
translations.idiomatic: Jin reported the victory and requested the man's promotion; Emperor Taizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，開寶中，太祖令有司造宅賜進，悉用筒瓦。

translations.literal: At first, in Kaibao, Emperor Taizu ordered the relevant offices to build a residence to grant Jin, using entirely tube tiles.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaibao, Emperor Taizu ordered a residence built for Jin using tube tiles throughout.

sentences.zh: 有司言：「舊制，非親王公主之第不可用。

translations.literal: The relevant offices said: "By old regulation, tube tiles may not be used except for the residences of imperial princes and princesses."
translations.idiomatic: The officials said, "By old regulation, tube tiles may be used only for imperial princes and princesses."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒曰：「進控扼西山十餘年，使我無北顧憂。

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Jin has controlled and held the western mountains for more than ten years, enabling me to have no worry looking north."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said, "Jin has held the western mountains for more than ten years and freed me from worry in the north.

sentences.zh: 我視進豈減兒女耶？

translations.literal: Do I regard Jin as less than my own children?
translations.idiomatic: Do I value Jin less than my own children?

sentences.zh: 亟往督役，無妄言。

translations.literal: Go quickly and supervise the work — no idle talk.
translations.idiomatic: Go supervise the work at once — no more idle talk."

sentences.zh: 」太平興國初，又賜宅一區。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, another residence was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo another residence was granted to him.

sentences.zh: 附 牛思進

translations.literal: Appendix: Niu Sijin
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Niu Sijin

sentences.zh: 牛思進者，祁州無極人。

translations.literal: Niu Sijin was a man of Wuji in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sijin was a native of Wuji in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 少從軍，以膂力聞。

translations.literal: In youth he joined the army and was known for physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the army young and was known for his strength.

sentences.zh: 嘗取強弓絓於耳，以手引之令滿。

translations.literal: He once took a strong bow, hooked it on his ear, and drew it to the full with his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He once hooked a strong bow on his ear and drew it to the full with one hand.

sentences.zh: 又負牆立，力士二人撮其乳曳之，嶷不動，軍中咸異之。

translations.literal: Again, standing with his back to a wall, two strong men grasped his nipples and pulled him — he did not move; all in the army marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Standing back to a wall, two strong men grasped his chest and pulled — he did not budge; the whole army marveled.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，知平定軍，從征河東，石嶺關部署郭進卒，命思進代之。

translations.literal: In year four of Taiping Xingguo, he governed Pingding Army; following the Hedong campaign, when Shiling Pass commander Guo Jin died, Sijin was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo year four he governed Pingding Army; after Guo Jin died at Shiling Pass during the Hedong campaign, Sijin replaced him.

sentences.zh: 師還，以功改本州團練使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, for merit he was changed to regimentation commissioner of his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned he was made regimentation commissioner of his prefecture for his service.

sentences.zh: 七年，授右千牛衛上將軍致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In year seven, he was granted retirement as upper general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he retired as upper general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and died.

sentences.zh: 李謙溥

translations.literal: Li Qianpu
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianpu

sentences.zh: 李謙溥，字德明，幷州盂人。

translations.literal: Li Qianpu, courtesy name Deming, was a man of Yu in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianpu, courtesy name Deming, was a native of Yu in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 性慷慨，重然諾。

translations.literal: By nature he was generous and valued keeping his word.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous by nature and valued his word.

sentences.zh: 父蕘，後唐清泰中，晉祖鎮幷門，署為參謀。

translations.literal: His father Rao, in Qingtai of Later Tang when the Jin ancestor was stationed at Bingmen, was appointed as staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rao, during Later Tang's Qingtai era when the Jin founder was posted at Bingmen, served as staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 天福初，為開封府推官，使契丹還，上言：「屈節外國，非久長策。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, he was judicial aide of the Kaifeng prefecture; returning from an mission to the Khitan, he submitted a memorial: "Bowing to a foreign state is not a long-term strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianfu he was judicial aide of Kaifeng prefecture; returning from a Khitan mission he memorialized, "Bowing to a foreign state is no long-term strategy."

sentences.zh: 」時晉祖方父事契丹，不悅其言，出為汝州魯山令，卒官。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin ancestor was just treating the Khitan as a father-lord and was displeased with his words; he was sent out as magistrate of Lushan in Ru prefecture and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder, then treating the Khitan as overlord, disliked this and sent him out as magistrate of Lushan in Ru prefecture, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 謙溥少通《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: Qianpu in youth mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Qianpu mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals in youth.

sentences.zh: 從晉祖入汴，補殿直，奉使契丹。

translations.literal: Following the Jin ancestor into Bian, he was appointed palace attendant and sent on mission to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Jin founder into Bian, he became palace attendant and served as envoy to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，改西頭供奉官，漢初，遷東頭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shaodi acceded, he was changed to western head tribute officer; at the beginning of Han he was transferred to eastern head.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shaodi took the throne he became western head tribute officer; early in Later Han he was transferred to eastern head.

sentences.zh: 周祖討三叛及守鄴都，謙溥往來宣密命，周祖愛之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Zhou campaigned against the Three Rebellions and guarded Ye capital, Qianpu went back and forth conveying secret orders; the Zhou founder favored him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou's founding emperor campaigned against the Three Rebellions and held Ye capital, Qianpu carried secret orders back and forth and won his favor.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，遷供備庫副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun, he was transferred to deputy commissioner of the supply depot.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun era he became deputy commissioner of the supply depot.

sentences.zh: 世宗征劉崇，遼州刺史張乙堅壁不下，遣謙溥單騎說之，乙以城降，以功改閑廄使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned against Liu Chong, Zhang Yi, prefect of Liao prefecture, held the walls and would not surrender; Qianpu was sent alone on horseback to persuade him, and Yi surrendered the city; for merit he was changed to commissioner of the idle stables.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Liu Chong, Emperor Shizong sent Qianpu alone on horseback to persuade Zhang Yi, prefect of Liao, who held the walls; Yi surrendered, and Qianpu was made commissioner of the idle stables.

sentences.zh: 師還，留為晉州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was retained as Jinzhou horse and foot army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was kept on as Jinzhou horse and foot supervisor.

sentences.zh: 以偏師入河東境，頻致克捷，世宗詔褒美之。

translations.literal: With a detached force he entered Hedong territory and repeatedly achieved victories; Emperor Shizong issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Leading a detached force into Hedong he won repeated victories, and Emperor Shizong issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 會隰州刺史孫義卒，時世宗親征淮南，謙溥謂節帥楊廷璋曰：「大寧，咽喉要地，不可闕守。

translations.literal: When Sun Yi, prefect of Xi prefecture, died, at the time Emperor Shizong was personally campaigning in Huainan; Qianpu said to military governor Yang Tingzhang: "Daning is a vital throat-point and must not be left undefended."
translations.idiomatic: When Xi prefect Sun Yi died while Emperor Shizong was campaigning in Huainan, Qianpu told military governor Yang Tingzhang, "Daning is a vital choke point and must not be left undefended."

sentences.zh: 且車駕出征，若俟報，則孤城陷矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, with the imperial carriage on campaign, if we wait for a report, the isolated city will fall.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor on campaign, waiting for orders would mean the isolated city falls.

sentences.zh: 」廷璋即署謙溥權隰州事。

translations.literal: Tingzhang immediately appointed Qianpu to provisional charge of Xi prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhang immediately put Qianpu in provisional charge of Xi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至郡，亟命浚城隍，嚴兵備，凡八日，幷人果以數千騎來寇。

translations.literal: Reaching the prefecture, he urgently ordered the moat and walls dredged and defenses tightened; within eight days the men of Bing indeed came to raid with several thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the prefecture he urgently dredged the moat, strengthened defenses, and within eight days Jin forces raided with several thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時盛暑，謙溥單衣持扇，從二小吏登城，徐步按視戰具。

translations.literal: It was peak summer heat; Qianpu in light clothing holding a fan, followed by two junior clerks, mounted the wall and slowly walked inspecting battle equipment.
translations.idiomatic: In peak summer heat Qianpu mounted the wall in light clothing with a fan, followed by two clerks, and slowly inspected the battle equipment.

sentences.zh: 幷人退舍，後旬餘，大發衝車攻城。

translations.literal: The men of Bing withdrew; after more than ten days they launched battering rams on a large scale to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin forces withdrew; more than ten days later they returned with battering rams.

sentences.zh: 謙溥募敢死士，得百餘人，短兵堅甲，銜枚夜縋出城。

translations.literal: Qianpu recruited dare-to-die soldiers, obtaining more than a hundred men with short weapons and strong armor, gagged and lowered by rope from the wall at night.
translations.idiomatic: Qianpu recruited more than a hundred dare-to-die soldiers with short weapons and strong armor, gagged and lowered from the wall by rope at night.

sentences.zh: 會廷璋兵至，合勢夾攻，掩其不及。

translations.literal: When Tingzhang's troops arrived, they combined forces in a pincer attack and caught them unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhang's troops arrived they pincered the enemy and caught them unprepared.

sentences.zh: 幷人大擾，悉眾遁去。

translations.literal: The men of Bing were greatly thrown into disorder and fled with their entire force.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin forces were thrown into disorder and fled with their entire army.

sentences.zh: 追北數十里，斬首千餘級，時顯德四年也。

translations.literal: Pursuing north for several tens of li, more than a thousand heads were cut off; this was in year four of Xiande.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing north for tens of li they counted more than a thousand heads; this was Xiande year four.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，攻破孝義縣，以功領衢州刺史、監軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year, he captured Xiaoyi county; for merit he held the post of prefect of Qu prefecture while retaining army supervision as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following fifth month he captured Xiaoyi county and for his service held the post of Qu prefecture prefect while retaining army supervision.

sentences.zh: 世宗北征，召赴行在。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned north, he was summoned to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong marched north he was summoned to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，為澶州巡檢使，詔城莫州，數旬而就。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gongdi acceded, he became Danzhou patrol inspector; an edict ordered the building of Mo prefecture's walls, completed within several tens of days.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gongdi took the throne he became Danzhou patrol inspector; ordered to build Mo prefecture's walls, he finished in several weeks.

sentences.zh: 改丹州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Dan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Dan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，移慈州，兼晉、隰緣邊都巡檢，行石州事，以興同砦為治所。

translations.literal: In year four of Jianlong, he was transferred to Ci prefecture, concurrently serving as overall frontier patrol inspector of Jin and Xi, conducting Shi prefecture affairs, with Xingtong stockade as his seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong year four he was transferred to Ci prefecture as overall frontier patrol inspector of Jin and Xi, governing Shi prefecture affairs from Xingtong stockade.

sentences.zh: 冬，將有事於南郊。

translations.literal: That winter, there was to be a ceremony at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: That winter a southern suburb ceremony was planned.

sentences.zh: 太祖命四路進兵，略地太原。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu ordered four routes to advance troops and seize territory around Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu ordered four columns to advance and seize territory around Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 鄭州刺史孫延進、絳州刺史沈繼深、通事舍人王睿等師出陰地，以謙溥為先鋒，會霍邑。

translations.literal: Sun Yanjin, prefect of Zheng prefecture, Shen Jishen, prefect of Jiang prefecture, palace attendant Wang Rui, and others led troops out from Yindi; Qianpu was made vanguard and they joined at Huoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yanjin of Zheng prefecture, Shen Jishen of Jiang prefecture, palace attendant Wang Rui, and others marched from Yindi with Qianpu as vanguard, joining at Huoyi.

sentences.zh: 謙溥因畫攻取之策，繼深等共沮之，延進不能用。

translations.literal: Qianpu therefore drew up a plan for attack and capture; Jishen and others jointly obstructed it, and Yanjin could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: Qianpu drew up an attack plan, but Jishen and others blocked it and Yanjin would not adopt it.

sentences.zh: 軍還，出白璧關，次谷口，謙溥語諸將曰：「王師深入敵境，今既退軍，彼必乘我，諸君當備之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, exiting Baiyu Pass and halting at Gukou, Qianpu said to the generals: "The imperial army has penetrated deep into enemy territory; now that we have withdrawn, they will surely seize upon us — you gentlemen must prepare."
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, exiting Baiyu Pass and halting at Gukou, Qianpu told the generals, "We have penetrated deep into enemy territory; on withdrawal they will surely pursue — prepare yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」諸將不答，謙溥獨令所部擐甲。

translations.literal: The generals did not reply; Qianpu alone ordered his command to don armor.
translations.idiomatic: The generals said nothing; Qianpu alone ordered his troops to don armor.

sentences.zh: 俄追騎果至，延進等倉皇走谷中，獨謙溥麾兵拒之，幷人引退。

translations.literal: Soon pursuing cavalry indeed arrived; Yanjin and others fled in panic into the valley, while Qianpu alone commanded troops to resist them, and the men of Bing withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing cavalry soon arrived; Yanjin and others fled panic-stricken into the valley while Qianpu alone held them off and the Jin forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移隰州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to prefect of Xi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Xi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，召謙溥為濟州團練使。

translations.literal: In year three of Kaibao, Qianpu was summoned as Jizhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao year three Qianpu was summoned as Jizhou regimentation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 後邊將失律，復為晉、隰緣邊巡檢使，邊民聞之喜，爭相迎勞於道左。

translations.literal: Later when frontier generals lost discipline, he was again made Jin and Xi frontier patrol inspector; frontier people hearing of it rejoiced and competed to welcome and comfort him on the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier generals lost discipline he was again made Jin and Xi frontier patrol inspector; border residents rejoiced and lined the roads to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 六年，領兵入太原，連拔七砦。

translations.literal: In year six, he led troops into Taiyuan and captured seven stockades in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he led troops into Taiyuan and captured seven stockades in succession.

sentences.zh: 八年，以疾求歸，肩輿抵洛，太祖遣中使領太醫就視之。

translations.literal: In year eight, because of illness he requested to return; carried in a sedan chair he reached Luoyang, and Emperor Taizu sent an inner attendant leading imperial physicians to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, ill, he requested to return; carried in a sedan he reached Luoyang, and Emperor Taizu sent an inner attendant with imperial physicians.

sentences.zh: 至京師，疾篤，累上章辭祿，不許。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital, his illness was severe; he repeatedly submitted memorials declining salary, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the capital gravely ill, he repeatedly asked to resign his salary but was refused.

sentences.zh: 明年春，卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: The next spring he died at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚痛惜之，賻贈有加，葬事官給。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu deeply grieved and regretted it; burial gifts were increased and funeral affairs were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu deeply mourned him, increased the burial gifts, and supplied the funeral at state expense.

sentences.zh: 謙溥與宣祖同里閈，弟謙升與太祖為布衣交。

translations.literal: Qianpu was from the same neighborhood as the Imperial Ancestor; his younger brother Qiansheng was a commoner's friend of Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Qianpu was from the same neighborhood as the Imperial Ancestor; his younger brother Qiansheng had been Emperor Taizu's friend since their commoner days.

sentences.zh: 其母閻嘗厚待太祖，及即位，數迎入宮中，使左右掖之，不令拜，命坐飲食，話及舊故，賜齎優厚。

translations.literal: His mother Yan had once treated Emperor Taizu generously; upon his accession he repeatedly welcomed her into the palace, had attendants support her, did not allow her to bow, ordered her seated for food and drink, spoke of old times, and granted generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Yan had once treated Emperor Taizu generously; after his accession Taizu repeatedly welcomed her to the palace, had attendants support her, forbade her to bow, seated her for meals, reminisced, and gave lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，太宗為許王納謙升女為夫人，以謙升為如京副使。

translations.literal: In Yongxi, Emperor Taizong took Qiansheng's daughter as consort for the Prince of Xu and made Qiansheng deputy envoy to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi, Emperor Taizong took Qiansheng's daughter as consort for the Prince of Xu and made Qiansheng deputy envoy to the capital.

sentences.zh: 謙溥子允則、允正。

translations.literal: Qianpu's sons were Yunze and Yunzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qianpu had sons Yunze and Yunzheng.

sentences.zh: 允則至寧州防禦使。

translations.literal: Yunze rose to defense commissioner of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yunze rose to defense commissioner of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 從子允恭為內殿崇班、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: His nephew Yun'gong served in the Inner Hall Honored Corps and as gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Yun'gong served in the Inner Hall Honored Corps and as gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 子 允正

translations.literal: Son: Yunzheng
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yunzheng

sentences.zh: 允正，字修己，以蔭補供奉官。

translations.literal: Yunzheng, courtesy name Xiuji, entered office by privilege as a tribute officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzheng, courtesy name Xiuji, entered office by privilege as a tribute officer.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，掌左藏庫，屢得升殿奏事，太宗頗記憶其舊故。

translations.literal: In Taiping Xingguo he managed the left treasury, repeatedly gained audience to report affairs, and Emperor Taizong quite remembered their old connection.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo he managed the left treasury, repeatedly reported at audience, and Emperor Taizong remembered their old connection.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，與張平同掌三班，俄為閤門祗候。

translations.literal: In Yongxi he jointly managed the three ranks with Zhang Ping and soon became a gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he jointly managed the three ranks with Zhang Ping and soon became a gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷閤門通事舍人。

translations.literal: In year four he was transferred to gate palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became gate palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時女弟適許王，以居第質於宋偓，太宗詰之曰：「爾父守邊二十餘年，止有此第耳，何以質之？

translations.literal: At the time his younger sister was married to the Prince of Xu; he had pledged the family residence to Song Wo; Emperor Taizong questioned him: "Your father guarded the frontier for more than twenty years and had only this residence — why pledge it?"
translations.idiomatic: His younger sister was married to the Prince of Xu; he had pledged the family residence to Song Wo; Emperor Taizong asked, "Your father guarded the frontier for more than twenty years and owned only this house — why pledge it?"

sentences.zh: 」允正具以奏，即遣內侍輦錢贖還，縉紳咸賦詩頌美。

translations.literal: Yunzheng fully reported the details; the emperor immediately sent an inner attendant with a cart of cash to redeem it, and officials all composed poems praising the act.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzheng explained fully; the emperor sent an inner attendant with cash to redeem it, and officials composed poems praising the act.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，命討戎、瀘州叛蠻。

translations.literal: In Chunhua he was ordered to suppress rebellious tribes in Rong and Lu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua he was ordered to suppress rebellious tribes in Rong and Lu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遷西上閤門副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to western upper gate deputy envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He became western upper gate deputy envoy.

sentences.zh: 太宗慮京城獄囚淹繫，命允正提總之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong feared that capital prisoners were detained too long and ordered Yunzheng to oversee them overall.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing capital prisoners were detained too long, Emperor Taizong put Yunzheng in overall charge.

sentences.zh: 嘗請詔御史臺給開封府司錄司、左右軍巡、四排岸司印紙作囚簿，署禁繫月日，條其罪犯，歲滿較其殿最。

translations.literal: He once requested an edict that the Censorate supply Kaifeng prefecture's record office, left and right military patrol offices, and four pier patrol offices with sealed paper to make prisoner registers, noting dates of detention, listing crimes, and comparing performance at year's end.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the Censorate supply Kaifeng offices with sealed registers noting detention dates and crimes, with annual performance reviews.

sentences.zh: 詔從其請。

translations.literal: An edict acceded to his request.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 逾年，開封府上言：「京師浩穰，禁繫尤眾，御史府考較之際，胥吏奔命，有妨推鞫，況無欺隱，不煩推校。

translations.literal: After a year, Kaifeng prefecture submitted a memorial: "The capital is vast and crowded, and detainees are especially numerous; when the censorate compares records, clerks run themselves ragged, hindering interrogation; moreover there is no concealment — detailed verification is unnecessary."
translations.idiomatic: A year later Kaifeng prefecture reported, "The capital is crowded with detainees; censorate reviews overwork the clerks and hinder interrogation; there is no concealment — detailed verification is unnecessary."

sentences.zh: 」卒罷之。

translations.literal: It was finally abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The system was finally abolished.

sentences.zh: 允正又提點左右藏，屢乘傳北面，經度邊要。

translations.literal: Yunzheng also supervised the left and right treasuries, repeatedly traveling by relay post to the north to manage frontier strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzheng also supervised the left and right treasuries and repeatedly traveled north by relay post to manage frontier strategic points.

sentences.zh: 五年，為衛州修河部署。

translations.literal: In year five he was river-repair commander of Wei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was river-repair commander of Wei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會建清遠軍積石砦，命詣瀚海部分其役。

translations.literal: When Qingyuan Army's Jishi stockade was being built, he was ordered to go to the Hanhai to allocate the labor.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingyuan Army's Jishi stockade was being built, he was sent to the Hanhai to allocate the labor.

sentences.zh: 還，拜西上閤門使、幷州駐泊鈐轄。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed western upper gate envoy and Bingzhou garrison military controller.
translations.idiomatic: On return he became western upper gate envoy and Bingzhou garrison military controller.

sentences.zh: 俄代張永德知州事，徙代州。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Zhang Yongde in governing the prefecture and was transferred to Dai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He soon replaced Zhang Yongde as prefect and was transferred to Dai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，使西蜀詢訪民事，還，進秩東上閤門使，歷知鎮、莫二州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was envoy to western Shu to inquire into civilian affairs; on return he was advanced to eastern upper gate envoy and successively governed Zhen and Mo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he was envoy to western Shu to inquire into civilian affairs; on return he was promoted to eastern upper gate envoy and governed Zhen and Mo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又為幷、代馬步軍鈐轄。

translations.literal: He also served as Bing and Dai horse and foot army military controller.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Bing and Dai horse and foot military controller.

sentences.zh: 契丹擾邊，車駕駐大名，允正與高瓊率太原軍出土門路來會，召見便殿。

translations.literal: When the Khitan harassed the frontier, the imperial carriage was stationed at Daming; Yunzheng and Gao Qiong led the Taiyuan army out through Tumen route to join, and he was summoned to audience in the side hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan harassed the frontier and the emperor was at Daming, Yunzheng and Gao Qiong led the Taiyuan army through Tumen route to join him and he was received in the side hall.

sentences.zh: 所部有廣銳騎士數百，皆素練習，命允正引以入，賜緡錢。

translations.literal: His command had several hundred Broad Sharp cavalry, all well trained; he was ordered to lead them in and was granted cash.
translations.idiomatic: His command included several hundred well-trained Broad Sharp cavalry; he was ordered to lead them in and was rewarded with cash.

sentences.zh: 遣屯邢州，與石保吉逐遼人，遼人遁去。

translations.literal: He was sent to garrison Xingzhou; with Shi Baoji he drove off the Liao people, and they fled.
translations.idiomatic: Posted at Xingzhou, he and Shi Baoji drove off the Liao forces.

sentences.zh: 俄以兵會大名，復還幷代。

translations.literal: Soon he joined forces at Daming and returned again to Bing and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the forces at Daming and returned to Bing and Dai.

sentences.zh: 五年，合涇原儀渭、邠寧環慶兩路為一界，命王漢忠為都部署，驛召允正為鈐轄兼安撫都監，即日上道。

translations.literal: In year five, the Jingyuan-Yiwei and Binning-Huanqing two routes were combined into one frontier; Wang Hanzhong was ordered as overall commander; Yunzheng was summoned by courier as military controller and concurrent pacification supervisor and set out the same day.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Jingyuan-Yiwei and Binning-Huanqing routes were combined; Wang Hanzhong was made overall commander and Yunzheng was summoned by courier as military controller and pacification supervisor, setting out the same day.

sentences.zh: 又命與錢若水同詣洪德、懷安沿邊諸砦經度邊事，加領誠州刺史。

translations.literal: He was also ordered with Qian Ruoshui to go to Hongde, Huaian, and other frontier stockades to manage frontier affairs, and additionally given charge of Cheng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With Qian Ruoshui he was sent to Hongde, Huaian, and other frontier stockades to manage border affairs and was additionally given charge of Cheng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七月，罷兩路之職，復任幷代鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the two-route posts were abolished and he was again appointed Bing and Dai military controller.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the two-route posts were abolished and he returned as Bing and Dai military controller.

sentences.zh: 每錢若水按巡邊壘，即詔權蒞州事。

translations.literal: Whenever Qian Ruoshui inspected frontier fortifications, an edict ordered Yunzheng to provisionally hold prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Qian Ruoshui inspected frontier fortifications, Yunzheng was ordered to provisionally govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 進四方館使，代馬知節為鄜延部署、兼知延州，改客省使、知定州兼鎮定都鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to envoy of the Four Directions Hall, replaced Ma Zhijie as Yan-Yan commander with concurrent governance of Yanzhou, was changed to guest reception envoy, and governed Dingzhou with concurrent overall military control of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to envoy of the Four Directions Hall, he replaced Ma Zhijie as Yan-Yan commander and governor of Yanzhou, then became guest reception envoy and prefect of Dingzhou with overall military control of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，累表求還。

translations.literal: In year three of Dazhong Xiangfu, he repeatedly submitted memorials requesting to return.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu year three he repeatedly asked to return to court.

sentences.zh: 至京師，將祀汾陰，以疾難於扈從，命為河陽部署以便養。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital, when the Fenyin sacrifice was about to be performed, because of illness he had difficulty accompanying the retinue and was ordered to be Heyang commander for convenient recuperation.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the capital, too ill to join the Fenyin sacrifice, he was made Heyang commander for recuperation.

sentences.zh: 會張崇貴卒，趙德明頗逾軼，亟詔徙允正為鄜延部署，內侍密詔存諭。

translations.literal: When Zhang Chonggui died and Zhao Deming grew quite overbearing, an urgent edict transferred Yunzheng as Yan-Yan commander; an inner attendant conveyed a secret edict of encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chonggui died and Zhao Deming grew overbearing, Yunzheng was urgently transferred as Yan-Yan commander with a secret edict of encouragement from an inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 禮成，領河州團練使。

translations.literal: When the rite was completed, he held the post of Hezhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the rite he became Hezhou regimentation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 允正頗知書，性嚴毅，疏財，喜自修飭。

translations.literal: Yunzheng was quite learned, stern and resolute by nature, free with wealth, and fond of self-cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzheng was learned, stern, generous, and fond of self-discipline.

sentences.zh: 素病佝僂，以是罕在要近，累典邊任，多殺戮。

translations.literal: He had long suffered from hunchback; therefore he was rarely in key posts close to court, but repeatedly held frontier duties and killed many.
translations.idiomatic: A lifelong hunchback kept him from key court posts, but he repeatedly held frontier duties and was quick to kill.

sentences.zh: 是秋，徙知永興軍，卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: That autumn he was transferred to govern Yongxing Army and died at age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was transferred to govern Yongxing Army and died at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 姚內斌

translations.literal: Yao Neibin
translations.idiomatic: Yao Neibin

sentences.zh: 姚內斌，平州盧龍人。

translations.literal: Yao Neibin was a man of Lulong in Ping prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Neibin was a native of Lulong in Ping prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仕契丹為關西巡檢、瓦橋關使。

translations.literal: Serving the Khitan, he was Guanxi patrol inspector and Waqiao Pass commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the Khitan he was Guanxi patrol inspector and commissioner of Waqiao Pass.

sentences.zh: 周顯德六年，太祖從世宗北征，兵次瓦橋關，內斌率眾五百人以城降。

translations.literal: In year six of Xiande of Zhou, Emperor Taizu followed Emperor Shizong on the northern campaign; when troops halted at Waqiao Pass, Neibin led five hundred men to surrender the city.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou's Xiande year six, when Emperor Taizu followed Emperor Shizong north and halted at Waqiao Pass, Neibin surrendered the city with five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 世宗以為汝州刺史，吏民詣闕舉留，恭帝詔褒之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong made him prefect of Ru prefecture; officials and people went to court recommending he be retained, and Emperor Gongdi issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong made him prefect of Ru prefecture; officials and residents petitioned at court to keep him, and Emperor Gongdi issued a praising edict.

sentences.zh: 內斌本名犯宣祖諱下一字，遂改今名。

translations.literal: Neibin's original name violated the character below the taboo of the Imperial Ancestor, so he changed to his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Neibin's original name violated a taboo on the Imperial Ancestor's name, so he changed to his present name.

sentences.zh: 從平李筠，改虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Following in pacifying Li Jin, he was changed to prefect of Guo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After helping pacify Li Jin he became prefect of Guo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 西夏數犯西鄙，以內斌為慶州刺史兼青、白兩池榷鹽制置使。

translations.literal: Western Xia repeatedly violated the western frontier; Neibin was made prefect of Qing prefecture with concurrent duty as salt monopoly commissioner of the Green and White pools.
translations.idiomatic: As Western Xia repeatedly raided the west, Neibin was made Qing prefecture prefect and salt monopoly commissioner of the Green and White pools.

sentences.zh: 在郡十數年，西夏畏伏，不敢犯塞，號內斌為「姚大蟲」，言其武猛也。

translations.literal: In the prefecture for more than ten years, Western Xia feared and submitted, not daring to violate the passes, and called Neibin "Big Bug Yao," speaking of his martial fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years in office Western Xia feared him and dared not raid the frontier, calling him "Big Bug Yao" for his martial fierceness.

sentences.zh: 初，內斌降，其妻子皆在契丹。

translations.literal: At first when Neibin surrendered, his wife and children were all with the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: When Neibin first surrendered, his wife and children were still with the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，子承贊密自幽州來歸。

translations.literal: In year four of Qiande, his son Chengzan secretly came from Youzhou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande year four his son Chengzan secretly came from Youzhou to join him.

sentences.zh: 五年，幽州民田光嗣等又以內斌兒女六人間道來歸，太祖並召見，賜以衣服、緡錢、鞍馬，令中使護送還內斌。

translations.literal: In year five, Youzhou residents Tian Guangsi and others also brought Neibin's six children and grandchildren by secret route to surrender; Emperor Taizu summoned them all, granted clothing, cash, and saddle horses, and ordered an inner attendant to escort them back to Neibin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Youzhou residents led six of Neibin's children and grandchildren by secret route to join him; Emperor Taizu received them, granted clothing, cash, and horses, and sent an inner attendant to escort them to Neibin.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，召赴闕，上待之甚厚，遣歸治所。

translations.literal: In year four of Kaibao he was summoned to court; the emperor treated him very generously and sent him back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao year four he was summoned to court, treated generously, and sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 七年春，暴得疾卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the spring of year seven he suddenly fell ill and died at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he suddenly fell ill and died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 遣中使護喪，歸葬洛陽，常賻外，賜其子田三十頃。

translations.literal: An inner attendant was sent to oversee the funeral; he was buried in Luoyang; beyond the regular burial gifts, thirty qing of fields were granted to his son.
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant oversaw the funeral; he was buried in Luoyang; beyond regular burial gifts, thirty qing of fields were granted to his son.

sentences.zh: 承贊為供奉官、閤門祗候，死於陣；

translations.literal: Chengzan served as tribute officer and gate attendant and died in battle;
translations.idiomatic: Chengzan served as tribute officer and gate attendant and died in battle;

sentences.zh: 承鑒至殿中丞。

translations.literal: Chengjian rose to palace director.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjian rose to palace director.

sentences.zh: 董遵誨

translations.literal: Dong Zunhui
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zunhui

sentences.zh: 董遵誨，涿州范陽人。

translations.literal: Dong Zunhui was a man of Fanyang in Zhuo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zunhui was a native of Fanyang in Zhuo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父宗本，善騎射，隸契丹帥趙延壽麾下，嘗以事說延壽，不能用。

translations.literal: His father Zongben was skilled in horsemanship and archery, served under Khitan commander Zhao Yanshou, and once advised Yanshou on affairs but was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zongben was skilled in horsemanship and archery, served under Khitan commander Zhao Yanshou, and once offered advice that Yanshou ignored.

sentences.zh: 及延壽被執，舉族南奔。

translations.literal: When Yanshou was captured, the whole clan fled south.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshou was captured the whole clan fled south.

sentences.zh: 漢祖得之，擢拜隨州刺史，署遵誨隨州牙校。

translations.literal: The Han ancestor obtained him, promoted and appointed him prefect of Sui prefecture, and appointed Zunhui to a Suizhou guard staff post.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder took him in, made him prefect of Sui prefecture, and appointed Zunhui to the Suizhou guard staff.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，世宗北征，大將高懷德，遵誨之舅也，表遵誨從行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande of Zhou, when Emperor Shizong campaigned north, the great general Gao Huaide, Zunhui's maternal uncle, memorialized that Zunhui accompany the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhou's Xiande era, when Emperor Shizong marched north, great general Gao Huaide, Zunhui's maternal uncle, recommended that Zunhui accompany the campaign.

sentences.zh: 師次高平，與晉人遇。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Gaoping, they encountered the men of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Gaoping they encountered Jin forces.

sentences.zh: 將接戰，晉兵未成列，懷德命遵誨先出奇兵擊之，晉人潰，大軍繼進，遂敗之。

translations.literal: About to join battle, Jin troops had not yet formed ranks; Huaide ordered Zunhui to lead a surprise force to strike first; the Jin men routed; the main army followed and they defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: As battle was about to begin, the Jin forces had not yet formed their ranks. Huaide ordered Zunhui to lead a surprise detachment against them first. The Jin troops broke and fled, the main army pressed forward, and they were defeated.

sentences.zh: 二年，討秦、鳳，大將韓通又表遵誨自隨。

translations.literal: In year two, attacking Qin and Feng, great general Han Tong again memorialized that Zunhui accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, during the campaign against Qin and Feng prefectures, great general Han Tong again recommended that Zunhui accompany him.

sentences.zh: 與賊戰於唐倉，先登陷陣，擒蜀招討使王鸞以獻，克秦、鳳二州。

translations.literal: They fought the enemy at Tangcang; he was first to climb and break the formation; he captured Shu pacification commissioner Wang Luan and presented him; he took the two prefectures of Qin and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: They fought the enemy at Tangcang. Zunhui was the first to scale the walls and break the enemy formation, captured the Shu pacification commissioner Wang Luan and presented him as a prize, and took both Qin and Feng prefectures.

sentences.zh: 師還，錄其前後功，補東西班押班，又遷驍武指揮使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his merits before and after were recorded; he was appointed to the east and west ranks escort corps; he was further promoted to commander of Xiao Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, his earlier and later achievements were recorded. He was appointed to the east and west ranks escort corps and was further promoted to commander of the Xiao Wu guard.

sentences.zh: 四年，從世宗征淮南，攻合肥，下之。

translations.literal: In year four, he followed Emperor Shizong on the Huainan campaign, attacked Hefei, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he accompanied Emperor Shizong on the Huainan campaign, attacked Hefei, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 六年，從韓通平雄、霸二州。

translations.literal: In year six, he followed Han Tong in pacifying the two prefectures of Xiong and Ba.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Han Tong in pacifying Xiong and Ba prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太祖微時，客遊至漢東，依宗本，而遵誨憑藉父勢，太祖每避之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu was still obscure, he traveled as a guest to Handong and relied on Zongben, but Zunhui relied on his father's power, and Taizu always avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu was still obscure, he traveled as a guest to Handong and lived under Zongben's roof, but Zunhui traded on his father's influence, and Taizu always kept his distance.

sentences.zh: 遵誨嘗謂太祖曰：「每見城上紫雲如蓋，又夢登高臺，遇黑蛇約長百尺餘，俄化龍飛騰東北去，雷電隨之，是何祥也？

translations.literal: Zunhui once said to Taizu: "Every time I see on the city walls purple clouds like a canopy, and I dreamed of climbing a high terrace and encountering a black serpent about a hundred feet long that soon transformed into a dragon and flew away toward the northeast, with thunder and lightning following. What kind of omen is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zunhui once said to Taizu, "Time and again I have seen purple clouds on the city walls like a canopy, and I dreamed that I climbed a high terrace and met a black serpent about a hundred feet long that suddenly turned into a dragon and soared away to the northeast, with thunder and lightning in its wake. What omen could this be?"

sentences.zh: ”」太祖皆不對。

translations.literal: "」Emperor Taizu to all of it did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: To all of this, Emperor Taizu made no reply.

sentences.zh: 他日論兵戰事，遵誨理多屈，拂衣而起。

translations.literal: Another day when discussing military matters, Zunhui was often bested in argument; he swept his robes and rose.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, when they discussed military affairs, Zunhui was repeatedly worsted in argument and swept his robes aside and stalked off.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃辭宗本去，自是紫雲漸散。

translations.literal: Taizu then took leave of Zongben and departed; from then on the purple clouds gradually dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then took leave of Zongben and departed, and from that time the purple clouds gradually faded away.

sentences.zh: 及即位，一日，便殿召見，遵誨伏地請死，帝令左右扶起，因諭之曰：「卿尚記往日紫雲及龍化之夢乎？

translations.literal: When he took the throne, one day in the informal palace hall he summoned Zunhui; Zunhui prostrated himself and begged for death; the Emperor ordered attendants to help him up and instructed him: "Do you still remember the purple clouds and the dragon-transformation dream of those days?"
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, one day he summoned Zunhui to the informal palace hall. Zunhui prostrated himself and begged for death. The Emperor ordered attendants to help him up and said, "Do you still remember the purple clouds and the dream of the dragon's transformation from those days?"

sentences.zh: 」遵誨再拜呼萬歲。

translations.literal: "Zunhui bowed twice and cried ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Zunhui bowed twice and cried, "Long live the Emperor!"

sentences.zh: 俄而部下有軍卒擊登聞鼓，訴其不法十餘事，太祖釋不問。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward a soldier under his command beat the drum of direct appeal, accusing him of more than ten unlawful acts; Taizu released him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a soldier under his command beat the drum of direct appeal to the throne and accused him of more than ten unlawful acts, but Taizu dismissed the charges without investigation.

sentences.zh: 遵誨益惶愧待罪，太祖召而諭之曰：「朕方赦過賞功，豈念舊惡耶？

translations.literal: Zunhui grew even more fearful and ashamed, awaiting punishment; Taizu summoned and instructed him: "I am now pardoning faults and rewarding merit—why would I bear old grudges?"
translations.idiomatic: Zunhui grew still more fearful and ashamed, awaiting punishment. Taizu summoned him and said, "I am now pardoning past faults and rewarding merit—why would I dwell on old grievances?"

sentences.zh: 汝可勿復憂，吾將錄用汝。

translations.literal: You need not worry further; I shall employ you according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: You need worry no more. I intend to employ you according to your merits.

sentences.zh: 」遵誨再拜感泣。

translations.literal: "Zunhui bowed twice and wept with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Zunhui bowed twice and wept with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 又問遵誨：「母安在？

translations.literal: He also asked Zunhui: "Where is your mother?"
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Zunhui, "Where is your mother?"

sentences.zh: 」遵誨奏曰：「母氏在幽州，經患難睽隔。

translations.literal: "Zunhui reported: "My mother is in Youzhou, separated by hardship and disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Zunhui replied, "My mother is in Youzhou, separated from me by hardship and long distance."

sentences.zh: 」太祖因令人賂邊民，竊迎其母，送與遵誨。

translations.literal: "Taizu therefore had border people bribed to secretly escort his mother and delivered her to Zunhui.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then had border people bribed to smuggle his mother out and sent her to Zunhui.

sentences.zh: 遵誨遣外弟劉綜貢馬以謝，太祖解其所服真珠盤龍衣，命齎賜之。

translations.literal: Zunhui sent his younger maternal cousin Liu Zong to present horses in thanks; Taizu removed the pearl dragon robe he was wearing and ordered it sent as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Zunhui sent his younger maternal cousin Liu Zong to present horses in thanks. Taizu removed the pearl dragon robe he was wearing and ordered it sent as a gift.

sentences.zh: 綜曰：「遵誨人臣，豈敢當此。

translations.literal: Zong said: "Zunhui is a subject—how dare he accept this."
translations.idiomatic: Zong said, "Zunhui is a subject—how could he accept such a gift?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「吾方委以方面，不此嫌也。」

translations.literal: "Taizu said: "I am about to entrust him with a frontier command; I have no such scruples about this."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "I am about to entrust him with a frontier command—I have no such scruples about this."

sentences.zh: 會李筠叛澤、潞，令遵誨從慕容延釗討之，遷馬軍都軍頭，因留之鎮守。

translations.literal: When Li Jin rebelled in Ze and Lu, Zunhui was ordered to follow Murong Yanzhao to suppress him; he was promoted to army director of the horse corps and was then left to garrison the area.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jin rebelled in Ze and Lu, Zunhui was ordered to follow Murong Yanzhao to suppress him. He was promoted to army director of the horse corps and was then left behind to garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 三年，召歸，再遷為散員都虞候。

translations.literal: In year three he was recalled and was again promoted to corps deputy director of the scattered staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled and promoted again to corps deputy director of the scattered staff.

sentences.zh: 乾德六年，以西夏近邊，授通遠軍使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiande, because Western Xia was near the border, he was appointed commissioner of Tongyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qiande, because Western Xia lay close to the border, he was appointed commissioner of Tongyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 遵誨既至，召諸族酋長，諭以朝廷威德，刲羊釃酒，宴犒甚至，眾皆悅服。

translations.literal: When Zunhui arrived, he summoned the tribal chieftains, instructed them in the court's majesty and virtue, slaughtered sheep and poured wine, and feasted and rewarded them generously; all were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zunhui arrived, he summoned the tribal chieftains, explained the court's majesty and benevolence, slaughtered sheep and poured wine, and feasted and rewarded them lavishly. All were pleased and submitted.

sentences.zh: 後數月，復來擾邊，遵誨率兵深入其境，擊走之，俘斬甚眾，獲羊馬數萬，夷落以定。

translations.literal: Several months later they again came to raid the border; Zunhui led troops deep into their territory, routed them, captured and killed many, seized tens of thousands of sheep and horses, and the foreign settlements were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later they raided the border again. Zunhui led troops deep into their territory, drove them off, captured and killed a great many, seized tens of thousands of sheep and horses, and the frontier tribes were pacified.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其功，就拜羅州刺史，使如故。

translations.literal: Taizu commended his merit and appointed him on the spot as prefect of Luo; he continued in his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu commended his achievement and appointed him on the spot as prefect of Luo, while he continued in his former post.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，兼領靈州路巡檢。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he additionally served as inspector of the Lingzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Zunhui additionally served as inspector of the Lingzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 遵誨不知書，豁達無崖岸，多方略，能挽強命中，武藝皆絕人。

translations.literal: Zunhui did not know books; he was open and frank without edge or precipice; he had many stratagems; he could draw a strong bow and hit his mark; in martial arts he surpassed all.
translations.idiomatic: Zunhui was unlettered, open and unpretentious, and full of stratagems. He could draw a heavy bow and hit his mark, and in martial skill he surpassed everyone.

sentences.zh: 在通遠軍凡十四年，安撫一面，夏人悅服。

translations.literal: At Tongyuan Army for fourteen years altogether, he pacified his frontier sector and the Xia people were pleased to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He spent fourteen years altogether at Tongyuan Army, pacifying his sector of the frontier until the Xia people willingly submitted.

sentences.zh: 嘗有剽略靈武進奉使鞍馬、兵器者，遵誨部署帳下欲討之。

translations.literal: Once some raided the saddle-horses and weapons of an envoy bringing tribute to Lingwu; Zunhui deployed men from his staff to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Once bandits plundered the horses and weapons of an envoy bearing tribute to Lingwu. Zunhui deployed men from his staff to punish them.

sentences.zh: 夏人懼，盡歸所略，拜伏請罪，遵誨即慰撫令去。

translations.literal: The Xia people feared this, returned everything they had seized, kowtowed and begged forgiveness; Zunhui immediately comforted them and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia people were afraid, returned everything they had taken, kowtowed and begged forgiveness, and Zunhui immediately reassured them and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 自是各謹封略，秋毫不敢犯。

translations.literal: From then on each kept strictly to their borders and dared not violate even the slightest thing.
translations.idiomatic: From then on each side kept strictly to its borders and dared not trespass even in the slightest.

sentences.zh: 歷太祖、太宗朝，委遇始終不替，許以便宜制軍事。

translations.literal: Through the reigns of Emperors Taizu and Taizong, the trust shown him never diminished; he was permitted to handle military affairs at his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Through the reigns of Emperors Taizu and Taizong, the favor shown him never wavered, and he was permitted to handle military affairs at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo he died at age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo he died at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 帝軫悼久之，遣中使護葬，賵賻加等，錄其子嗣宗、嗣榮為殿直。

translations.literal: The Emperor mourned him deeply for a long time, sent an inner attendant to oversee the burial, increased the funeral gifts, and appointed his sons Sizong and Sirong as palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor mourned him at length, sent an inner attendant to oversee the funeral, increased the funeral gifts, and appointed his sons Sizong and Sirong as palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 賀惟忠

translations.literal: He Weizhong
translations.idiomatic: He Weizhong

sentences.zh: 賀惟忠，忻州定襄人。

translations.literal: He Weizhong was a man of Dingxiang in Xin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He Weizhong was a native of Dingxiang in Xin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少勇敢，善騎射。

translations.literal: As a youth he was brave and skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was brave and skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 周祖將兵討三叛，惟忠謁於道左，自陳其有武藝，周祖悅之，即留置所部。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder was about to lead troops against the three rebellions, Weizhong presented himself on the roadside and declared his martial skills; the Zhou founder was pleased and immediately kept him in his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder was about to lead troops against the three rebellions, Weizhong presented himself by the roadside and declared his martial skills. The Zhou founder was pleased and immediately kept him in his command.

sentences.zh: 洎開國，得隸世宗帳下，奏補供奉官，不辭，輒入朝。

translations.literal: When the state was founded he came under Emperor Shizong's retinue; he petitioned to be appointed tribute officer and, without waiting for reply, entered court.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was founded he came under Emperor Shizong's retinue. He petitioned to be appointed tribute officer and, without waiting for a reply, entered court.

sentences.zh: 世宗怒之，及嗣位，終不遷擢。

translations.literal: Shizong was angry at him; when he succeeded to the throne he never promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was angry with him, and when he succeeded to the throne he never promoted him.

sentences.zh: 初授儀鸞副使，令知易州，捍邊有功，尋遷正使。

translations.literal: Initially he was appointed deputy commissioner of the Ceremonial Guard and ordered to govern Yi prefecture; he had merit defending the border and soon was promoted to full commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed deputy commissioner of the Ceremonial Guard and ordered to govern Yi prefecture. He distinguished himself defending the border and was soon promoted to full commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，太祖駐常山，以惟忠為本州刺史兼易、定、祁等州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, Taizu was stationed at Changshan and made Weizhong prefect of Ben prefecture while also making him inspector-in-chief of Yi, Ding, Qi and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao, Taizu was stationed at Changshan and made Weizhong prefect of Ben prefecture while also appointing him inspector-in-chief of Yi, Ding, Qi, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 嘗中流矢，六年，金瘡發而卒。

translations.literal: He had once been struck by a flowing arrow; in year six the old wound reopened and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He had once been struck by an arrow in battle. In the sixth year the old wound reopened and he died.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之嗟悼，即以其子昭度為供奉官。

translations.literal: When Taizu heard of it he sighed in grief and immediately appointed his son Zhaodu as tribute officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu heard of it he sighed in grief and immediately appointed his son Zhaodu as tribute officer.

sentences.zh: 惟忠性剛果，知書，洞曉兵法，有方略。

translations.literal: Weizhong was stern and resolute by nature; he knew books; he was thoroughly versed in military methods and had strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong was stern and resolute by nature. He was literate, thoroughly versed in military methods, and full of strategic insight.

sentences.zh: 在易州繕完亭障，撫士卒，得其死力，每乘塞用兵，所向必克，威名震北邊，故十餘年間契丹不敢南牧。

translations.literal: At Yi prefecture he repaired the pavilions and barriers, comforted the troops and won their utmost loyalty; whenever he took the field in border warfare he invariably prevailed; his renown shook the northern frontier, so for more than ten years the Khitan did not dare drive south to pasture.
translations.idiomatic: At Yi prefecture he repaired the watchtowers and barriers, treated his soldiers well, and won their utmost loyalty. Whenever he took the field on the border he invariably prevailed, and his renown shook the northern frontier, so for more than ten years the Khitan did not dare drive their herds south.

sentences.zh: 昭度至西京作坊使。

translations.literal: Zhaodu rose to workshop commissioner of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu rose to workshop commissioner of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，知通遠軍，有罪當棄市，減死流商州。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era he governed Tongyuan Army; guilty of a crime meriting execution, his sentence was reduced to exile in Shang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era he governed Tongyuan Army. Guilty of a capital crime, his sentence was reduced to exile in Shang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 馬仁瑀

translations.literal: Ma Renyu
translations.idiomatic: Ma Renyu

sentences.zh: 馬仁瑀，大名夏津人。

translations.literal: Ma Renyu was a man of Xiajin in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Renyu was a native of Xiajin in Daming.

sentences.zh: 十餘歲時，其父令就學，輒逃歸。

translations.literal: When he was about ten years old, his father sent him to study, but he always fled home.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about ten years old, his father sent him to school, but he always ran away home.

sentences.zh: 又遣於鄉校習《孝經》，旬餘不識一字。

translations.literal: He was again sent to a village school to study the "Classic of Filial Piety"; after more than ten days he did not know a single character.
translations.idiomatic: His father sent him again to a village school to study the "Classic of Filial Piety," but after more than ten days he could not recognize a single character.

sentences.zh: 博士笞之，仁瑀夜中獨往焚學堂，博士僅以身免。

translations.literal: The teacher flogged him; Renyu went alone at night to burn the schoolhouse, and the teacher barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: The teacher flogged him. Renyu went alone in the night to burn down the schoolhouse, and the teacher barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 常集里中群兒數十人，與之戲，為行陣之狀，自稱將軍，日與之約，鞭其後期者，群兒皆畏伏。

translations.literal: He often gathered several dozen neighborhood boys and played with them in the form of marching formations, calling himself general; every day he made appointments with them and flogged those who were late; all the boys feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He often gathered several dozen neighborhood boys to play war games with him in marching formation, calling himself general. Every day he set appointments with them and flogged those who were late, and all the boys feared and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 又市果均給之，益相親附。

translations.literal: He also bought fruit and distributed it equally among them, and they grew even more attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: He also bought fruit and distributed it equally among them, and they grew still more attached to him.

sentences.zh: 及長，善射，挽弓二百斤。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was skilled at shooting and could draw a two-hundred-jin bow.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he was skilled at archery and could draw a two-hundred-jin bow.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，周祖鎮鄴，仁瑀年十六，願隸帳下，周祖素聞其勇，既見，甚喜，留置左右。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou period of Han, the Zhou founder was stationed at Ye; Renyu was sixteen and wished to join his retinue; the Zhou founder had long heard of his courage; when they met he was greatly pleased and kept Renyu at his side.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou period of Han, the Zhou founder was stationed at Ye. Renyu was sixteen and wished to join his retinue. The Zhou founder had long heard of his courage, and when they met he was greatly pleased and kept Renyu at his side.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，補內殿直。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed to the inner palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed to the inner palace guard.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，命衛士習射苑中，仁瑀弓力最勁，而所發多中，賜錦袍、銀帶。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne he ordered the guard to practice archery in the garden; Renyu's bow strength was the greatest and most of his shots hit; he was rewarded with a brocade robe and silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne he ordered the guard to practice archery in the imperial garden. Renyu's bow strength was the greatest and most of his shots hit the mark, and he was rewarded with a brocade robe and silver belt.

sentences.zh: 會太原劉崇入寇，世宗親征至高平，周師不利，諸將多引退。

translations.literal: When Liu Chong of Taiyuan invaded, Shizong personally campaigned to Gaoping; Zhou forces fared badly and many generals withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong of Taiyuan invaded, Shizong personally marched to Gaoping. The Zhou forces fared badly and many generals fell back.

sentences.zh: 仁瑀謂眾曰：「主辱臣死，安用我輩！

translations.literal: Renyu said to the crowd: "When the lord is shamed the minister must die—what use are we!"
translations.idiomatic: Renyu said to those around him, "When the lord is shamed the minister must die—of what use are we!"

sentences.zh: 」乃控弦躍馬，挺身出陣射賊，斃者數十人，士氣益振，大軍乘之，崇遂敗績。

translations.literal: "Then he spanned his bow, leapt on his horse, thrust himself out of the formation to shoot the enemy, felling dozens; morale surged; the main army pressed the advantage and Chong was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Then he strung his bow, leapt on his horse, and thrust himself out of the formation to shoot at the enemy, felling dozens. Morale surged, the main army pressed the advantage, and Chong was utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 世宗至上黨，諸將坐失律誅者七十餘人。

translations.literal: Shizong reached Shangdang; more than seventy generals who had violated discipline were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong reached Shangdang, and more than seventy generals were executed for dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 擢仁瑀為弓箭控鶴直指揮使，及還京，又遷散指揮使。

translations.literal: Renyu was promoted to commander of the archer Crane Direct guard and, upon returning to the capital, was further promoted to commander of the scattered guard.
translations.idiomatic: Renyu was promoted to commander of the archer Crane Direct guard, and upon returning to the capital he was further promoted to commander of the scattered guard.

sentences.zh: 從征淮南，至楚州，攻水砦。

translations.literal: He followed the Huainan campaign to Chuzhou and attacked the river fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Huainan campaign to Chuzhou and attacked the river fortresses.

sentences.zh: 砦中建飛樓高百尺餘，世宗觀之，相去殆二百步，樓上望卒厲聲嫚罵，世宗怒甚，命左右射之，遠莫能及。

translations.literal: The fortress had a flying tower more than a hundred feet high; Shizong viewed it from about two hundred paces away; lookouts on the tower cursed loudly in abuse; Shizong was furious and ordered those at his side to shoot but none could reach that far.
translations.idiomatic: The fortress had a flying tower more than a hundred feet high. Shizong observed it from about two hundred paces away. Lookouts on the tower shouted abuse at him in harsh voices. Shizong was furious and ordered those at his side to shoot, but none could reach that far.

sentences.zh: 仁瑀引滿，應弦而顛。

translations.literal: Renyu drew the bow to the full; the man toppled at the sound of the string.
translations.idiomatic: Renyu drew his bow to the full, and the man toppled at the sound of the string.

sentences.zh: 及淮南平，身被數十創，賜以良藥，遷內殿直都虞候。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified he bore dozens of wounds; he was given fine medicine and promoted to deputy director of the inner palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified he had suffered dozens of wounds. He was given fine medicine and promoted to deputy director of the inner palace guard.

sentences.zh: 又從平三關。

translations.literal: He also followed in pacifying the Three Passes.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed in pacifying the Three Passes.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，詔從太祖北伐。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded, an edict ordered him to follow Taizu on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, an edict ordered him to follow Taizu on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 初以佐命功授散員都指揮使，領貴州刺史，俄遷鐵騎右廂都指揮使，又為虎捷左廂都指揮使，領扶州團練使。

translations.literal: Initially for his contribution in establishing the dynasty he was appointed commander of the scattered staff corps and given concurrent appointment as prefect of Gui; soon he was promoted to commander of the right wing of Iron Cavalry; he also became commander of the left wing of Tiger Fierce and concurrent prefect of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: For his contribution in establishing the dynasty he was first appointed commander of the scattered staff corps and given concurrent appointment as prefect of Gui. Soon he was promoted to commander of the right wing of Iron Cavalry, then became commander of the left wing of Tiger Fierce and concurrent prefect of Fu.

sentences.zh: 從平澤、潞，以功領常州防禦使，改龍捷左廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Ze and Lu; for his merit he was given concurrent post as defense commissioner of Changzhou and was changed to commander of the left wing of Dragon Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in pacifying Ze and Lu. For his merit he was given concurrent appointment as defense commissioner of Changzhou and was transferred to commander of the left wing of Dragon Fierce.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，改領岳州防禦使，俄又移領漢州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was changed to defense commissioner of Yue; soon he was moved to Han prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong he was transferred to defense commissioner of Yue, and soon afterward was moved to Han prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，詔仁瑀等領荊湖諸郡，不數歲，復其地。

translations.literal: Initially an edict had Renyu and others govern the Jing-Hu prefectures; within several years they recovered the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Initially an edict had Renyu and others govern the Jing-Hu prefectures, and within several years they recovered the territory.

sentences.zh: 至是，將征蜀，又詔領川、峽諸郡，遂平之。

translations.literal: At this point, as Shu was to be attacked, he was again ordered to govern the Chuan and Xia prefectures, and they pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: At this point, as Shu was about to be attacked, he was again ordered to govern the Chuan and Xia prefectures, and they pacified it.

sentences.zh: 先是，薛居正知貢舉，仁瑀私囑所與者，榜出，無其人。

translations.literal: Earlier Xue Juzheng had supervised the examinations; Renyu privately asked a favor for someone he knew; when the list was published that person was not on it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xue Juzheng had supervised the examinations. Renyu privately asked a favor for someone he knew, but when the list of successful candidates was published that person was not on it.

sentences.zh: 聞喜宴日，仁瑀酒酣，攜所囑者詣居正切責之。

translations.literal: On the day of the banquet of rejoicing over the results, Renyu, deep in his cups, took the person he had asked for and went to Xue Juzheng to rebuke him sharply.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the banquet celebrating the examination results, Renyu, deep in his cups, took the man he had recommended and went to Xue Juzheng to rebuke him sharply.

sentences.zh: 為御史中丞劉溫叟所劾，帝優容之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Liu Wensou impeached him; the Emperor treated him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Liu Wensou impeached him, but the Emperor treated him leniently.

sentences.zh: 王繼勳以后族驕恣，淩蔑將帥，人皆引避。

translations.literal: Wang Jixun, on account of being imperial kin by marriage, was arrogant and insolent and looked down on generals; everyone avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jixun, as a member of the imperial family by marriage, was arrogant and overbearing and looked down on generals, and everyone avoided him.

sentences.zh: 獨仁瑀詞氣不相下，嘗攘臂欲毆之。
