translations.literal: Only Renyu would not yield in tone; once he rolled up his sleeves wanting to beat him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Renyu would not yield to him in tone, and once rolled up his sleeves wanting to strike him.

sentences.zh: 會帝將講武郊外，遂欲相圖，各勒所部兵私市白梃。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to hold military exercises in the suburbs, they intended to set upon each other; each secretly had their troops buy white clubs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor was about to hold military exercises in the suburbs, they intended to settle matters by force, and each secretly had his troops buy white clubs.

sentences.zh: 太祖密知之，詔罷講武，出仁瑀為密州防禦使。

translations.literal: Taizu secretly learned of this, cancelled the exercises, and sent Renyu out as defense commissioner of Mi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu learned of this in secret, cancelled the exercises, and sent Renyu out as defense commissioner of Mi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖征晉陽，命仁瑀率師巡邊，至上谷、漁陽。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Jinyang he ordered Renyu to lead troops patrolling the border, reaching Shanggu and Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu campaigned against Jinyang he ordered Renyu to lead troops on a border patrol, reaching Shanggu and Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 契丹素聞仁瑀名，不敢出，因縱兵大掠，俘生口、牛羊數萬計。

translations.literal: The Khitan had long heard Renyu's name and did not dare come out; Renyu therefore let his troops plunder extensively, capturing people and cattle and sheep numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had long heard Renyu's name and did not dare come out, so Renyu let his troops plunder extensively, capturing people and cattle and sheep numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 駕還，仁瑀歸治所。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, Renyu went back to his administrative seat.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned, Renyu went back to his post.

sentences.zh: 明年，群盜起兗州，賊首周弼、毛襲甚勇悍，材貌奇偉，弼號曰「長腳龍」。

translations.literal: The next year bandits rose in Yan prefecture; the bandit leaders Zhou Bi and Mao Xi were very fierce and bold, of unusual build and appearance; Bi was called "Long-Legged Dragon."
translations.idiomatic: The next year bandits rose in Yan prefecture. The bandit leaders Zhou Bi and Mao Xi were very fierce and bold, of unusual stature and appearance, and Bi was called "Long-Legged Dragon."

sentences.zh: 監軍討捕數不利，詔仁瑀掩擊。

translations.literal: The military superintendent's punitive campaigns met repeated setbacks; an edict ordered Renyu to strike by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: The military superintendent's punitive campaigns met repeated setbacks, and an edict ordered Renyu to strike by surprise.

sentences.zh: 仁瑀率帳下十餘卒入泰山，擒弼，盡獲其黨，魯郊遂寧。

translations.literal: Renyu led a dozen-odd men from his retinue into Mount Tai, captured Bi, and seized his entire gang; the Lu region was thus pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Renyu led a dozen-odd men from his retinue into Mount Tai, captured Bi, and seized his entire gang, and the Lu region was thus pacified.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，遷瀛州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao he was transferred to defense commissioner of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao he was transferred to defense commissioner of Ying.

sentences.zh: 兄子嘗因醉誤殺平民，繫獄當死。

translations.literal: His brother's son once killed a commoner by mistake while drunk; he was imprisoned and faced death.
translations.idiomatic: His brother's son once killed a commoner by mistake while drunk and was imprisoned facing execution.

sentences.zh: 民家自言非有宿憾，但過誤爾，願以過失殺傷論。

translations.literal: The victim's family said they bore no old hatred—only a mistake—and wished it judged as accidental homicide.
translations.idiomatic: The victim's family said they bore no old grudge and that it was only a mistake, and they asked that it be judged as accidental homicide.

sentences.zh: 仁瑀曰：「我為長吏，而兄子殺人，此怙勢爾，非過失也。

translations.literal: Renyu said: "I am the senior official, and my brother's son killed a man—this is relying on power, not a mistake."
translations.idiomatic: Renyu said, "I am the senior official, and my brother's son killed a man. This is relying on power, not a mistake."

sentences.zh: 豈敢以私親而亂國法哉？

translations.literal: How could I let private kinship disrupt the laws of the state?
translations.idiomatic: How could I let private kinship disrupt the laws of the state?

sentences.zh: 」遂論如律，給民家布帛為棺斂具。

translations.literal: He therefore sentenced according to law and gave the victim's family cloth and silk for coffin and burial goods.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sentenced according to law and gave the victim's family cloth and silk for coffin and burial goods.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，移知遼州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to govern Liao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to govern Liao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，車駕征太原，命仁瑀與成州刺史慕容超、飛龍使白重貴、八作使李繼昇分兵攻城。

translations.literal: In year four, when the imperial carriage campaigned against Taiyuan, Renyu was ordered along with Cheng prefect Murong Chao, Flying Dragon envoy Bai Chonggui, and Eight Works commissioner Li Jisheng to divide forces and besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when the imperial carriage campaigned against Taiyuan, Renyu was ordered along with Cheng prefect Murong Chao, Flying Dragon envoy Bai Chonggui, and Eight Works commissioner Li Jisheng to divide their forces and besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 及征范陽，命仁瑀率禁兵擊契丹於盧龍北，契丹兵奔潰。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Fanyang, Renyu was ordered to lead palace guard troops to strike the Khitan north of Lulong, and the Khitan army fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: During the Fanyang campaign Renyu was ordered to lead palace guard troops against the Khitan north of Lulong, and the Khitan army fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 師還，遷朔州觀察使，判瀛州事。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was transferred to observation commissioner of Shuo prefecture with concurrent authority over Yingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he became Shuo prefecture observation commissioner with authority over Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，年五十。

translations.literal: In year seven he died at age fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died at fifty.

sentences.zh: 贈河西軍節度，葬事官給。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the Hexi military governorship, and funeral affairs were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Hexi military governor, and the state supplied the funeral.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋初，交、廣、劍南、太原各稱大號，荊湖、江表止通貢奉，契丹相抗，西夏未服。

translations.literal: The commentary says: At the beginning of Song, Jiao, Guang, Jiannan, and Taiyuan each claimed imperial titles; Jinghu and the lands south of the Yangzi only sent tribute; the Khitan stood in opposition, and Western Xia was not yet subdued.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: In the early Song, Jiao, Guang, Jiannan, and Taiyuan each claimed imperial titles; Jinghu and the south sent only tribute; the Khitan stood opposed, and Western Xia was not yet subdued.

sentences.zh: 太祖常注意於謀帥，命李漢超屯關南，馬仁瑀守瀛州，韓令坤鎮常山，賀惟忠守易州，何繼筠領棣州，以拒北敵。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu constantly paid attention to selecting commanders, ordering Li Hanchao to garrison Guannan, Ma Renyu to guard Yingzhou, Han Lingkun to hold Changshan, He Weizhong to defend Yi prefecture, and He Jiyun to command Di prefecture, to resist the northern enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu constantly focused on choosing commanders: Li Hanchao at Guannan, Ma Renyu at Yingzhou, Han Lingkun at Changshan, He Weizhong at Yi prefecture, and He Jiyun at Di prefecture — all to resist the northern enemy.

sentences.zh: 又以郭進控西山，武守琪戍晉州，李謙溥守隰州，李繼勳鎮昭義，以禦太原。

translations.literal: He also had Guo Jin control the western mountains, Wu Shouqi garrison Jin prefecture, Li Qianpu defend Xi prefecture, and Li Jixun hold Zhaoyi, to guard against Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He also posted Guo Jin on the western mountains, Wu Shouqi at Jin prefecture, Li Qianpu at Xi prefecture, and Li Jixun at Zhaoyi to guard against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 趙贊屯延州，姚內斌守慶州，董遵誨屯環州，王彥昇守原州，馮繼業鎮靈武，以備西夏。

translations.literal: Zhao Zan garrisoned Yanzhou, Yao Neibin guarded Qing prefecture, Dong Zunhui encamped at Huanzhou, Wang Yansheng defended Yuan prefecture, and Feng Jiye held Lingwu, to guard against Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zan was at Yanzhou, Yao Neibin at Qing prefecture, Dong Zunhui at Huanzhou, Wang Yansheng at Yuan prefecture, and Feng Jiye at Lingwu — all to guard against Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 其族在京師者，撫之甚厚。

translations.literal: Their clans in the capital were treated very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Their families in the capital were treated very generously.

sentences.zh: 郡中筦榷之利，悉以與之。

translations.literal: The profits from monopoly taxes in the prefectures were entirely given to them.
translations.idiomatic: All monopoly-tax profits in their prefectures were given to them.

sentences.zh: 恣其貿易，免其所過征稅，許其召募亡命以為爪牙。

translations.literal: They were allowed free trade, exempted from transit taxes, and permitted to recruit fugitives as their agents.
translations.idiomatic: They were allowed free trade, exempted from transit taxes, and permitted to recruit fugitives as their agents.

sentences.zh: 凡軍中事皆得便宜，每來朝，必召對命坐，厚為飲食，錫齎以遣之。

translations.literal: In all military affairs they were granted discretionary authority; whenever they came to court they were summoned to audience and ordered seated, given rich food and drink, and sent away with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In military affairs they had full discretion; whenever they came to court they were received in audience, seated, feasted, and sent away with gifts.

sentences.zh: 由是邊臣富貲，能養死士，使為間諜，洞知敵情；

translations.literal: From this frontier officials grew wealthy, able to maintain dare-to-die soldiers, employ them as spies, and thoroughly know enemy conditions;
translations.idiomatic: Thus frontier officials grew wealthy, maintained dare-to-die soldiers, employed spies, and knew the enemy thoroughly;

sentences.zh: 及其入侵，設伏掩擊，多致克捷，二十年間無西北之憂。

translations.literal: when the enemy invaded, they set ambushes and struck by surprise, often achieving victory, and for twenty years there was no worry in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: when enemies invaded they ambushed and struck by surprise, often winning victories, and for twenty years the northwest was secure.

sentences.zh: 以至命將出師，平西蜀，拓湖湘，下嶺表，克江南，所向遂志，蓋能推赤心以馭群下之所致也。

translations.literal: Thus when generals were ordered to march, they pacified western Shu, expanded Hunan and Hubei, descended to Lingnan, and conquered Jiangnan — wherever they went their aims were fulfilled; this was surely because he could extend sincere loyalty to command subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when generals marched forth they pacified western Shu, expanded Hunan and Hubei, took Lingnan, and conquered Jiangnan — succeeding wherever they went because Taizu commanded subordinates with sincere loyalty.

sentences.zh: 若李進卿、楊美亦專師西征，而美居北海，以樂易結民心，誠得為政之本。

translations.literal: As for Li Jinqing and Yang Mei, they also commanded armies westward; Mei governed Beihai with ease and pleasure, winning the people's hearts — truly grasping the root of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinqing and Yang Mei also led armies westward; Mei governed Beihai with ease and won the people's hearts — truly grasping the root of governance.

sentences.zh: 延渥、承矩、守恩、允正皆紹先業，以勳名著。

translations.literal: Yanwo, Chengju, Shou'en, and Yunzheng all continued their fathers' careers and were famed for their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwo, Chengju, Shou'en, and Yunzheng all continued their fathers' careers and won fame for their merit.

sentences.zh: 承矩議屯田，贊和好，其謀甚遠。

translations.literal: Chengju proposed garrison fields and praised good relations — his plans were very far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Chengju proposed garrison fields and favored good relations — his plans were far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 守恩以果敢死事。

translations.literal: Shou'en died in service through boldness and resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Shou'en died in service through boldness and resolution.

sentences.zh: 宋之武功，於斯為盛焉。

translations.literal: Song's military achievements were at their height in this.
translations.idiomatic: Song military achievement reached its height in this generation.
